title: Ahan Shetty to begin shooting for Sanki on October 30 in Bhopal
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
After Border 2, the star is set to return to the sets with a love story packed with emotions and raw action.

Adding to this, Written by Gyanendra Vasudev, Sanki will explore a love story at its core while incorporating raw and explosive action. The makers have kept the subject and storyline under wraps for now, with plans to reveal further details in due course. The movie is scheduled to arrive in theatres in the first half of 2027.

Meanwhile, Director Tinu Suresh Desai has already reached Bhopal with a large crew and is overseeing the final preparations ahead of the shoot. The production is expected to begin on October 30, marking Ahan’s next on-set outing following his appearance in Border 2 .

Notably, Following the response to Border 2 , Ahan has as per reports been selective about his next projects. Sanki will be among his soon-to-release releases, followed by Vikram Bhatt’s 1920 Cold Winter . The star is also expected to begin work on a couple of additional projects in 2027.

As per the latest buzz, The movie is backed by We The People, Roaring River Productions and Pals & Peers Entertainment. The project marks another step in Ahan’s career as he looks to build on the attention generated by his recent big-screen outing.

In further updates, While the makers have not disclosed further details about the characters or the plot, the combination of romance, emotional conflict and action is expected to form the movie’s central appeal. With the shooting schedule beginning in Bhopal, the production is now moving towards its next phase.

On top of that, Sanki is slated for a theatrical rollout in the first half of 2027. Further details about the movie, including its storyline and additional cast members, are expected to be revealed by the makers in the coming months.

title: Bhumi Pednekar reunites with Akshay Kumar for Priyadarshan’s next comedy
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Adding to this, The movie is as per reports set in the 1970s, with Akshay Kumar playing a tiger hunter. While details about the story are currently being kept under wraps, the project is being described as a comedy set against the period.

Meanwhile, Earlier reports had suggested that the movie could incorporate elements related to wildlife conservation alongside comedy and thriller elements. However, the makers have not revealed detailed plot information yet.

Notably, The movie is being produced by Ramesh Taurani. Reports have also suggested that Annu Kapoor and Rajpal Yadav could be part of the cast, although further details about their roles have not been officially disclosed.

As per the latest buzz, Bhumi and Akshay have previously shared screen space in Toilet: Ek Prem Katha and Raksha Bandhan . Their soon-to-release collaboration will therefore mark their third movie together.

In further updates, Raksha Bandhan , directed by Aanand L Rai, was rolled out in 2022 and featured Bhumi as Akshay’s co-star. The soon-to-release Priyadarshan project will bring the pair together in a different setting, with the story as per reports taking place several decades in the past.

On top of that, The movie is expected to begin production in the last week of November 2026. The shooting schedule is likely to span around three months, with Rajasthan and Mumbai among the locations. Bhopal is also being considered as a possible shooting location.

title: PVR INOX sees record Q2 as Indian box office crosses Rs 4,000 crore for FIRST time in a quarter!
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:
PVR INOX reports record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 2,133 crore rupees, with PAT up 111% and 46.3 million patrons amid strong Indian ticket-window growth.

Adding to this, For Q2 FY27, PVR INOX recorded revenue of Rs 21,327 million, or around Rs 2,133 crore rupees, on an Ind AS 116-adjusted basis. This marked a 17% increase from Rs 18,187 million in the corresponding quarter last year.

Meanwhile, Adjusted EBITDA rose 44% year on year to Rs 4,752 million, with the EBITDA margin improving to 22.3% from 18.1%. Profit after tax from continuing operations increased 111% to Rs 2,733 million, compared with Rs 1,296 million in Q2 FY26.

Notably, The cinema chain welcomed 46.3 million patrons during the quarter, marking a 4% year-on-year increase. Occupancy also improved to 30.4%, compared with 28.7% in the same period last year. Average ticket price rose 14% to Rs 298, while average food and beverage spending per head also increased 14% to Rs 153. Both ticketing and F&B revenues grew 18% during the quarter.
As per the latest buzz, The company shared the results were supported by a strong theatrical slate and increased consumer spending.

In further updates, Commenting on the performance, PVR INOX Managing Director Ajay Bijli shared, “Q2 FY'27 has been a landmark quarter for Indian cinema and PVR INOX. We achieved record quarterly and half-yearly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, supported by strong content, higher consumer spends and disciplined costs.”

On top of that, He added, “Our margins are now well above pre-COVID levels, a clear sign of a structurally stronger business. We generated significant free cash flow, completed our maiden share buyback and carry a strong balance sheet.”

PVR INOX's results come amid a strong quarter for the Indian theatrical market. According to Ormax Media and company estimates cited by PVR INOX, India's gross ticket-window collections reached Rs 4,443 crore rupees in Q2 FY27, representing 23% year-on-year growth.

title: Ranveer Singh's performance in Dhurandhar was more impactful than Ranbir Kapoor in Animal, feels Varun Dhawan
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor and Ranveer Singh have both impressed audiences with their performances in recent years, with Animal and Dhurandhar emerging as major box-office successes. But when asked to choose between the two actors for the more impactful performance, Varun Dhawan did not hesitate to pick a winner.

Adding to this, Varun Dhawan has a clear choice between Ranbir Kapoor and Ranveer Singh. Varun Dhawan picks between Ranveer Singh and Ranbir Kapoor The latest episode of Koffee With Karan Season 9 featured Janhvi Kapoor and Varun Dhawan as guests, with Arjun Kapoor joining them for the rapid-fire round. During the segment, Karan Johar asked Varun, "Ranveer Singh in Dhurandhar or Ranbir Kapoor in Animal, which one is a more impactful performance?" Without hesitation, Varun replied, "I would definitely say Ranveer in Dhurandhar."

Meanwhile, Interestingly, in the first episode of Koffee With Karan Season 9, Karan was asked to choose between Ranbir and Ranveer to decide who was the more versatile star. He responded, "You don't choose between brilliance."

Notably, Ranbir delivered one of the most talked-about performances of his career with Sandeep Reddy Vanga’s Animal (2023). Playing Ranvijay Singh, a man whose complicated relationship with his father drives him towards violence and revenge, the star showcased an intense side of his acting. Despite the movie facing criticism for its portrayal of women and glorification of toxic masculinity, his performance received widespread attention. Animal also became a major box-office success, collecting ₹ 915 crore rupees worldwide.

As per the latest buzz, Now, Ranbir is awaiting the rollout of Ramayana, a movie mounted on a massive budget of ₹ 4000 crore rupees. The mythological epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, also stars Sai Pallavi, Yash, Sunny Deol, and Ravie Dubey, among others. The movie will be rolled out in two parts, with the first one releasing on November 5, 2026.

In further updates, With Aditya Dhar’s Dhurandhar franchise, Ranveer moved away from his trademark flamboyance to deliver a restrained and intense performance. As Hamza Ali Mazari, an Indian spy operating undercover in Pakistan, Ranveer won over the followers with his performance and physical transformation. The franchise became a major box-office phenomenon. While Dhurandhar collected over ₹ 1300 crore rupees worldwide, Dhurandhar The Revenge became the first Indian movie to breach the ₹ 1000 crore rupees mark at the domestic ticket-window, earning ₹ 1800 crore rupees globally.

On top of that, As per the latest buzz, Varun will lead the next movie by Maamla Legal Hai director Rahul Pandey. The yet-untitled movie is shared to be backed by Karan Johar's Dharma Productions. title: Tanu Weds Manu 3 won't move ahead without R Madhavan and Kangana Ranaut, confirms Aanand L Rai, denies ‘fresh cast’ reports
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

There had been reports that a third Tanu Weds Manu movie was being planned with a ‘fresh’ cast. But now, filmmaker Aanand L Rai has put the speculations to rest. The director has shared that the third instalment of his hit romantic drama Tanu Weds Manu will not move ahead without its original leading actors, R Madhavan and Kangana Ranaut .

Adding to this, Tanu Weds Manu was rolled out in 2011. Aanand L Rai on Tanu Weds Manu 3 Aanand directed the first two films in the romantic-comedy franchise in 2011 and 2015. Both were commercial hits. Speaking with PTI in Mumbai, he shared, “Tanu Weds Manu won't be possible without Madhavan. So, whenever you will see any Tanu weds Manu, whether three or four or five, it will be with Madhavan and Kangana.”

Meanwhile, Earlier this year, there were reports that the third part of the movie was being planned with a fresh cast and an independent storyline. The original story revolved around an NRI who falls for the match his parents have arranged for him, but the woman has her heart set on another man.

Notably, Speaking on the sidelines of a movie festival in the city, the filmmaker also addressed whether Bollywood frequently succumbs to trends. Calling it a human reaction, the filmmaker advised makers to stick to their strengths. “You should know what your plus is or where you can score well. It's not great to repeat yourself, but at the same time, you should know that this is your world in which you can thrive. This is the world where you can discover something,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, Rolled out in 2011, Tanu Weds Manu starred Madhavan and Kangana as the titular characters, alongside Jimmy Sheirgill, Swara Bhasker, Deepak Dobriyal, and Eijaz Khan in key roles. A critical and commercial success, the movie collected ₹ 56 crore rupees on a ₹ 17-crore rupees budget. A sequel - Tanu Weds Manu Returns - was rolled out in 2015. This starred Kangana in dual roles. A massive ticket-window success, it minted over ₹ 250 crore rupees worldwide, and remains one of the biggest female-led box-office successes in Hindi cinema history. A third part has been speculated to be in development for some time now.

title: Netflix's Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh explains why polarising conversations are a better success metric than viewership numbers, top 10 lists | Interview
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

It has been a curious year for Netflix in India. The streaming platform has delivered some much-talked-about films, which have remained in public discourse for weeks after rollout. On the flip side, there are films that have grabbed the attention of the viewers immediately, like theatrical releases do. As the year winds down, we sit down to chat with Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh, Director, Original Films, Netflix India, on how 2026 was for films on Netflix and the idea of ‘success’ on streaming.

Adding to this, Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh discusses 2026 for films on Netflix and more. ‘The lead-up to rollout doesn't have to be rife’ ‘Surprising’ is the word that Ruchikaa uses to describe the year that Netflix films have had. “Every year, there's been one or two breakout titles that have really carried that conversation forward. I feel this year was surprising because, across the board, different films found success in their own right, which I haven't seen happen in a long time. Whether it was Accused, a small movie that travelled to 72 countries or Toaster, which was number one on the global top 10,” she says.

Meanwhile, Ruchikaa believes that streaming and the social media boom have changed how films ought to be promoted, at least a certain kind of movie. “Those days of promoting early on, creating a buzz are gone,” she says. “The lead-up to a movie doesn't have to be rife, given today's explosion of information. And we are so used to reading something today and then watching it immediately. That absolute call to action exists. There was a time when creating anticipation and excitement, and coming, were needed. And we’d have releases about they have started shooting, and they met outside this office. But, I think the audience can actually see through that today.”

Notably, It is often shared that streaming was a clutter-breaker for Indian cinema, as the films on OTT platforms broke the formulaic approach to filmmaking. Ruchikaa agrees, “Anything that feels formulaic has always been scary. I've handled theatrical (releases) for 12 years of my life. There would be proper formulaic films. And I used to be most scared. Because they would say, ‘Yeh to chal hi jaayegi (This will work for sure)’.”

As per the latest buzz, She agrees the industry has misunderstood what the audience wants, which is what gave rise to the formula. “When the audience really likes something, we say, ‘Let's give them some more of it’. Suddenly, what worked for something, you take that mould, and you make it a template, and it actually stops working. When we did Sector 36, we (were pitched) 20 true crime stories. But we've just done this, so this is exactly what we'll not do. The audience genuinely has shown us that they are ready. They say when you're ready to give us something new, and when you're taking those creative swings and risks, we are showing up,” she says.

In further updates, The years in India have helped Netflix understand what ‘success’ truly means for a movie away from the ticket-window. Ruchikaa says that while viewership figures and a place on global top lists are important, they aren’t everything. “Early on, it is important for me to see how many people are coming to it because I think that gives me a sense of whether we have been able to connect to people. But in the long term, I don't think it's ever going to be how many people have come and watched. Being in the global top 10 is incredible, and it is an important success metric. But for me, really, it is the conversation that sparks.”

On top of that, Ruchikaa says the conversations, especially the ones that are polarising, are what truly determine a movie’s success today. She explains, “When people watched Maa-Behen, there was a section that shared, ‘I feel represented.’ And then another section shared, "Ye kya tha? Auratein ye kya kar rahi hain?" And for me, both are very important conversations, because there are certain films that actually appeal to polarising conversations, and we encourage them because that is really how we find ourselves in the centre of the zeitgeist. So when a movie lives with you far after, when there are characters that you'll remember, when there are mannerisms you'll do, it means that something of that has stayed in you, and that truly is the measure of success for a movie for me.”

With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. title: Varun Dhawan wants Sidharth Malhotra for a Heated Rivalry remake, says there was tension in Student of the Year
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Varun Dhawan has a pick for a Bollywood version of Heated Rivalry , and it is none other than his Student of the Year co-star Sidharth Malhotra . The star made the suggestion on Karan Johar’s Koffee With Karan Season 9, joking that the two had the kind of tension that could have taken their 2012 movie in a very different direction. Varun Dhawan and Janhvi Kapoor were the guests on the third episode of the final season, along with Arjun Kapoor as special guest.

Adding to this, Varun Dhawan has a pick for a Bollywood version of Heated Rivalry, and it is none other than his Student of the Year co-star Sidharth Malhotra. Varun says followers wanted him and Sidharth to end up together The conversation came up during the rapid-fire round of an episode featuring Varun and Janhvi, with Arjun joining them on the couch midway. When Karan asked Varun which male co-star he would choose for a remake of the Canadian romance series, he was quick with his answer: “Sidharth Malhotra”.

Meanwhile, Karan, who launched both actors in Student of the Year, seemed to approve of the idea, calling the pairing “quite sexy”. Varun then explained why he thought it could work, bringing up the movie that first introduced him and Sidharth to audiences. He pointed out that their characters already had a certain dynamic in Student of the Year. “I think there was (sexual) tension (between them) even in SOTY,” he shared, adding, “Lot of people were, me and Sid should end up together more than Alia”.

Notably, The remark left Arjun wondering whether he had missed an alternate version of the 2012 movie. He asked if Student of the Year actually had such an ending, prompting Varun to insist that it did. Arjun then joked that the version Varun was talking about existed only in his imagination. In Student of the Year, Varun and Sidharth played students who find themselves competing against each other, with Alia Bhatt’s character caught up in the rivalry.

As per the latest buzz, The internet wasted no time reacting to Varun’s confession. Since the episode dropped, the clip has been doing the rounds on social media, particularly on X (formerly Twitter), where one post featuring the exchange has racked up nearly a million views. Followers have also been sharing edits of Rohan and Abhimanyu from Student of the Year, highlighting the tension between their characters and imagining what their dynamic might have looked like as a romance.

In further updates, Heated Rivalry centres on Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov, two professional hockey players whose rivalry on the ice slowly turns into a romance they keep hidden from the world. Adapted from Rachel Reid’s Game Changers novels, the Canadian series follows their relationship over a decade as they struggle to balance their feelings for each other with their careers and the pressure of being public figures.

On top of that, Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie play the two hockey stars, and the series has become a massive hit, turning both actors into breakout stars and bringing them a level of fame that has grown well beyond the show. Heated Rivalry premiered in India on Lionsgate Play in February 2026 in English and Hindi. With the series finding a huge global audience, the actors are now filming the second season, which is scheduled to rollout in 2027.

Varun is as per reports in talks to star in Yash Raj Films' first-ever horror feature movie, directed by Abhay Pannu. A source close to the project told Hindustan Times earlier this year, “Varun has come on board as the lead for YRF’s first horror movie. Yash Raj Films (YRF) is entering the horror genre for the first time.” If things fall into place, this will be the star's first collaboration with YRF since the 2018 slice-of-life drama Sui Dhaaga, which also starred Anushka Sharma.

title: Anupam Kher says he feels proud to see the reactions to Ramayana after its LA premiere; praises Namit Malhotra, Nitesh Tiwari and Ranbir Kapoor
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

All eyes are on Ramayana as it gears up for rollout in a few days. Ranbir Kapoor , Sai Pallavi, Yash and director Nitesh Tiwari attended the Los Angeles premiere of Ramayana at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. Following the grand premiere, the first reactions to the ambitious adaptation of the Indian epic surfaced on social media where many lauded its scale, visuals and performances, with comparisons being made to The Lord of the Rings.

Adding to this, Anupam Kher is awaiting the rollout of Ramayana. What Anupam Kher shared Now, veteran star Anupam Kher, who has voiced the vulture demigod Jatayu in the movie, has shared a note after the movie's premiere in LA. Anupam shared a video on X, saying he is really happy to see the reactions to Ramayana after the world premiere in Los Angeles. He added that the audience can see the grandeur and visuals, and that it is a moment of pride that an epic of India has been presented on this scale internationally. He lauded the combined effort of producer Namit Malhotra, director Nitesh Tiwari, music composers Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman and the entire cast and crew for their immense hard work in making Ramayana.

Meanwhile, He added, “People are also noticing the amazing creation of Jatayu in the movie, and it gives me so much pleasure to tell you that I have voiced that part. Actually, to see how Indian talent and Indian films are getting lauded outside the country gives me a lot of satisfaction. Thank you to the creators in Ramayana for taking the movie to such a grand scale. Go watch the movie when it releases in theatres on November 5.”

Notably, In the caption, he wrote in Hindi, “The early reactions to Ramayana coming in from Los Angeles are filling my heart with immense joy and pride. Seeing our great epic reach audiences around the world on such a grand scale is an incredible feeling. And in this journey, getting to voice Jatayu is especially meaningful to me. I'm eagerly looking forward to watching the movie in Stockholm on November 5. Jai Ho!”

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana. The cast also includes Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

In further updates, As per reports mounted on a budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees, the movie is backed by Yash and Namit Malhotra and is planned as a two-part franchise. The first instalment is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 5, 2026, with the second part expected to arrive around Diwali 2027.

title: Janhvi Kapoor finally confirms she is dating Shikhar Pahariya, reveals marriage plans on Koffee With Karan
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Bollywood star Janhvi Kapoor and Shikhar Pahariya have been rumoured to be dating for a long time. However, neither has publicly verified their relationship. Now, during her recent appearance on Koffee With Karan Season 9 , Janhvi has finally admitted to dating Shikhar and shared her plans for marriage.

Adding to this, Janhvi Kapoor confirms relationship with Shikhar Pahariya. Janhvi Kapoor on marriage plans with Shikhar Pahariya In the latest episode of Koffee With Karan, when Karan Johar asked Janhvi whether she was officially dating Shikhar, she verified it and added, "I always thought about why everyone is so cagey about it. Obviously I don't want nazar, and I don't want to be overly explicit about what's happening in my personal life. I just think it's overrated to be like 'let no one ever know'. So it's kind of boring to tiptoe around it, and it's not a big deal."

Meanwhile, Varun Dhawan also spoke about Janhvi's admiration for Shikhar, recalling how he once "baby-sat" the two of them during a turbulent flight. Karan also asked Janhvi about marriage, to which she gave a clear answer: “Not for another two-three years for sure.” She added that they were in a good place, despite break-ups happening all around them.

Notably, During the conversation, Janhvi also recalled Shikhar's support after her mother, Sridevi, died. She opened up that although they were not romantically involved at the time, Shikhar, who was studying in London, left halfway through his semester and returned to Mumbai to be by her side. She also opened up that Shikhar stayed with a friend in Juhu rather than at his own home so that he could be available to her whenever she needed him.

As per the latest buzz, Janhvi and Shikhar have known each other since their teens. title: Kunal Kapoor, who plays Indra Dev in Ramayana, says one of the biggest things holding India back is ‘our fear of failure’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Kunal Kapoor is gearing up for the rollout of Ramayana , where he plays Indra Dev. The star takes to his X account to often share candid thoughts and opinions on a variety of topics. He talks about the films he liked and the latest events in the country and interacts with users on the platform. On Thursday, the star shared a long note about how one of the biggest things that is holding India back is the fear of failure.

Adding to this, Kunal Kapoor spoke about the need to take risks and how one must not be afraid to fail. Kunal speaks on the shame attached to failure In his note, Kunal shared, “I think one of the biggest things holding India back is our fear of failure. We’re taught to fear it from the time we’re young. Students are pushed to breaking point because failing an exam feels like the end of the world. We stay in marriages everyone knows aren’t working because leaving feels like failure. People stay in jobs they hate because they’re terrified they won’t find another one. We’ve built a society where the shame of failing often feels worse than the cost of staying stuck.”

Meanwhile, The star then went on to add how this is a generational issue and cannot be cured so easily. He wrote, “And to be fair to us, it comes from generations of scarcity. Too many people, too few opportunities. When survival is the priority, taking risks feels like a luxury. But you cannot build a great country if its people are terrified of getting things wrong. We don’t just need more ambition. We need to become a country where failure isn’t a life sentence. And maybe that’s starts small, with how we react to our kids or people around us, when they fail.”

Notably, Kunal did not specifically point out any particular project or name anyone to share why he spoke about failure. When a fan commented, “Spoken like a true king, Lord Indra,” the star acknowledged the comment with folded hands emoticons.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana. The ensemble cast also includes Lara Dutta, Sunny Deol, Ravi Dubey, Sheeba Chaddha, and Arun Govil in key roles. The movie is slated for a two-part rollout, with the first part hitting cinemas on Diwali 2026 and the second in 2027.

In further updates, Earlier in an interview with News18, Kunal had spoken the large scale on which the movie is made and shared, “This is a very important movie in our cultural history. It’s a really important part of our cultural ethos. I think it’s important that we have filmmakers and teams who can give it the kind of scale it needs. This is mounted at a scale that we’ve never seen before.”

title: Tamannaah Bhatia is unbothered by Annu Kapoor's ‘misogynist’ remark on her complexion, says she's focused on work
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Annu Kapoor faced criticism last year for his comments on Tamannaah Bhatia 's complexion and appearance during a podcast, with his remarks being labelled misogynistic and sexist. Speaking at NDTV Profit Ignite, Tamannaah has now opened up that she was unbothered by his comments and remains focused on her work.

Adding to this, Tamannaah Bhatia reacts to Annu Kapoor's remark on her complexion. Tamannaah Bhatia replies to Annu Kapoor's remark When asked about the remarks on her complexion, which drew criticism for being misogynistic and sexist, Tamannaah was also asked whether her movie choices were part of an image makeover aimed at changing how audiences perceive her at this stage of her career, beyond her image as an star known for her screen presence and sensuality. She shared she was unbothered by the comments.

Meanwhile, She shared, "I think that as a creative person, our most important task is to listen. And when we listen, what we keep and what we filter is very important to understand. And because you are also a woman, you can understand that if we start giving importance to such things, then perhaps we will not be able to move forward in life."

Notably, She added, "So I don't even see these things. I focus on my work. I focus on what I want to make. I focus on my acting career. And genuinely, according to me, I want to do my work like a service. And I do that. And maybe that's why it reaches people, because somewhere it comes from the right place."

As per the latest buzz, Last year, Annu appeared on Shubhankar Mishra's YouTube channel and spoke about watching a clip of the song Aaj Ki Raat. The host then asked him whether he liked the song and mentioned that he admired Tamannaah. In response, Annu shared, "Mashallah kya dudhiya badan hai (Mashallah, what a fair and beautiful body)."

In further updates, Annu went on to say, "Behen, apne gaane se, aapne shareer se, apne dudhiya chehre se humare bacchon ko sulaati hain... Bahut achi baat hai.. Desh ke upar kripa hogi agar humare desh ke bacch achi aur swasth neend soyein. Agar aur bhi kuch ichcha hain toh bhagwan unko samarth karre ke unki ichcha puri hun (Our sister is making kids sleep with her song, with her milky face and body, if she is making our children sleep sweetly, it's very good, man... It will be a great blessing for this country that our children get a good and healthy night's sleep. If she has any other wishes, may God give her the capability to fulfil her wishes. That's my blessing for her)."

On top of that, Tamannaah was last seen in Vvaan: Force of the Forest, which also featured Sidharth Malhotra in a lead role. She will next be seen in Balaji Motion Pictures' Ragini MMS 3. The movie also stars Junaid Khan in a lead role and is scheduled for rollout in 2027.

title: Varun Dhawan regrets his ‘8 hits in a row’ boast against Ranbir Kapoor, Ranveer Singh on Koffee With Karan, says he jinxed his success
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Varun Dhawan once boasted about his successful films while addressing comparisons with Ranveer Singh and Ranbir Kapoor on Koffee With Karan Season 6. During his recent appearance on Koffee With Karan Season 9, the star admitted that he regretted the boast and expressed his desire to emulate Ajay Devgn.

Adding to this, Varun Dhawan says he shouldn't have flexed about his success. Varun Dhawan regrets flexing his success on Koffee With Karan 9 When Karan Johar spoke about Varun becoming a “meme factory” because of his smile, Varun shared that it was Karan who had started it. He further explained that the smile meme originated from a scene in Student of the Year. He added, “I think the whole thing of these things happening, whether it was a push narrative or not a push narrative, what I have realised over the time, after maturing, is that the only flex one should do is with your work. Like, I feel many years back, I came here and flexed about how many hits I had, and eventually, it jinxed me.”

Meanwhile, Karan then brought up Varun’s earlier statement about Ranbir and Ranveer. During Koffee With Karan Season 6, when Karan asked Varun who he considered a bigger competitor, Ranbir or Ranveer, Varun replied, “No one. they haven't had what I've had. I've had eight hits in a row.”

Notably, Varun and Janhvi Kapoor then pointed out that Varun had had 11 hits by that point, but he was quick to clarify that he did not want it to look like another boast. He added, “I don't want to flex or anything in that matter because I just feel that when you are having success or something becomes success, I think it is something better to be like Ajay Devgn. He doesn't react. He is that one guy I have seen through success or through failure; he looks at you the same way. It's amazing.”

As per the latest buzz, Varun was most of late seen in David Dhawan's Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, which collected only ₹ 74.83 crore rupees worldwide at the ticket-window and received negative reviews. He will as per reports headline the next movie by Maamla Legal Hai director Rahul Pandey. The yet-untitled movie is shared to be backed by Karan Johar's Dharma Productions. However, no official announcement has been made so far.

title: Sharvari dances with OG Rajshri heroine Madhuri Dixit to Yeh Prem Mol Liya song, calls it a ‘surreal’ moment with her idol
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Sharvari got to live a fan moment she will remember for a long time. The star of late danced with Madhuri Dixit to the title track of her soon-to-release movie, Yeh Prem Mol Liya , and shared a video of their meeting on Instagram. The movie stars Ayushmann Khurrana opposite Sharvari and is helmed by Sooraj Barjatya.

Adding to this, Sharvari calls Madhuri Dixit an OG Rajshri heroine. Sharvari calls Madhuri Dixit her idol In the video, Sharvari begins dancing to the song before Madhuri joins her. The two share a few steps, and the clip ends with Sharvari bowing to the veteran star before the two hug. The sweet interaction brings together two generations of actors connected to the Rajshri banner.

Meanwhile, Sharvari shared her excitement in the caption, thanking Madhuri for the warmth and affection she showed her. She also referred to the star as one of the original Rajshri heroines, recalling the legacy of the films she has been part of. Sharvari wrote, “So honoured to receive this much prem from one of the OG Rajshri heroines of Sooraj Barjatya sir.. the one and only Madhuri Dixit ma’am ♥️✨ Getting to dance alongside my idol feels surreal and soooo special 🥹😭♥️ Thankyou ma’am, you are the best! Hum Aapke Hain Kaun 🤝 #YehPremMolLiya In theatres 27th Nov 2026.”

Notably, View this post on Instagram Madhuri’s association with Sooraj Barjatya goes back to Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!, the 1994 smash hit that became known for its songs, family celebrations and memorable performances. The movie was led by her and Salman Khan along with Mohnish Bahl and Renuka Shahane in pivotal roles.

As per the latest buzz, The dance video comes as the makers build excitement around the movie’s music. Earlier this month, they rolled out Jhumka Patola, a pre-wedding song sung by Shreya Ghoshal and composed by Himesh Reshammiya.

In further updates, The star opened up about her experience filming Jhumka Patola and how the director helped her connect with her character through the music. She shared, “I’ve always loved dancing, but with Sooraj sir, a song is so deeply woven into the narrative that you can’t look at it as just a dance performance. While shooting ‘Jhumka Patola’, he would walk me through what the moment meant for my character and share stories from the songs he has made over the years, and I tried to carry that into every step and expression. Dance has its own language, and sometimes a song can say what a scene simply cannot.”

On top of that, Yeh Prem Mol Liya is produced by Rajshri Productions in association with Mahaveer Jain Films. The movie also features Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak, Seema Pahwa and Saumya Tandon. It is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 27, 2026.

title: Digital world isolates people, cinema offers collective experience, says Imtiaz Ali
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Filmmaker Imtiaz Ali believes the growing consumption of digital content has made people more isolated, while the big screen offers a shared emotional experience.

Adding to this, Digital world isolates people, cinema offers collective experience, says Imtiaz Ali "Post COVID, the viewing habits have changed. Today, people watch a lot more ... So, things have changed big time in the industry. Today, we're watching ten times more content in different forms, be it reels, stories, etc. But these things are often watched in isolation, either on a phone or on some other device, when you're alone," Ali shared last evening on day one of a movie festival here.
Meanwhile, The filmmaker shared the theatrical experience remains valuable because cinema allows people to share their reactions and emotions with others.

Notably, "When I'm experiencing something, like an emotion, and the people around me are experiencing the same thing, it gives a very beautiful feeling because humans were not created to live isolated from everyone," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, "However, the disadvantage of the digital world is that it isolates people, whereas the advantage of theatre is that it gives people a collective experience. I don't have a secret formula to give as to how a movie works but I hope films work in theatres and that people go to theatres to watch a movie. Like, it happened in case of 'Main Vaapas Aaunga'," Ali added.

In further updates, The director reflected on the response to his last movie, "Main Vaapas Aaunga", and shared achieving both critical appreciation and commercial success was a matter of good fortune.

On top of that, "The lesson that we got from this was that there should be a direct interaction between a filmmaker and audience, every filmmaker and artist should be connected to people, then they will know what more can they do in their respective field. Otherwise, we are taking a shot in the dark, and that's why our work sometimes does not hit the mark," Ali shared.
Asked about his next movie, the director shared he is currently writing a story and doesn't have actors in mind.

title: After SRFTI, Naseeruddin Shah shares video backing Jamia Millia Islamia students, says he is a 'proud dimagi Naxal'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After lending support to the students of the Satyajit Ray Movie and Television Institute (SRFTI), star Naseeruddin Shah has now come out in support of Jamia Millia Islamia students, who have been protesting for the restoration of their union.

Adding to this, Naseeruddin Shah has backed the protesting Jamia Millia Islamia students. Naseeruddin Shah backs Jamia students The multiple National Award winner shared a video on social media on Wednesday, slamming the central government for their reaction to the Jamia students' protests, and accused the BJP -led administration of trying to destroy the education system and break the "courage of the country's youth".

Meanwhile, In the video, the star appeared wearing a ‘Dimagi Naxal’ pin, showing it to the camera. The term was used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a speech earlier this year for critics of the administration.

Notably, "I proudly declare that I am Dimagi Naxal. I don't know what other nicknames the watchmen have given to people like me, anti-national, 'tukde tukde' gang, and I don't know what else," Naseeruddin Shah shared in Hindi.

As per the latest buzz, In the video, posted on Facebook, Naseer added, “I want to ask this government a question. What else will you do to break the courage of our country's youth, to destroy the education system, and to put our democracy at risk? How much will you do? How far will you go?”

In further updates, The 76-year-old star has been posting frequent videos and has been vocal in his support for student-related issues. He earlier criticised the government for its handling of the Cockroach Janata Party-led protest over NEET exam irregularities in July.
On top of that, The protesting students have demanded a definite date for the polls, which have not been held since 2006, and a clear timeline for the approval of the student union's constitution.

As protests at the Jamia Millia Islamia entered their 15th day on Monday, the administration agreed to one of the students' key demands, announcing it would resume student union elections after two decades. However, this failed to resolve the stand-off with students saying the administration had not issued a definite timeline for the polls.

title: Janhvi Kapoor's cheeky dating advice to Veer Pahariya on Koffee With Karan has internet calling it a dig at Tara Sutaria

Janhvi Kapoor's dating advice to Veer Pahariya In the latest episode, Janhvi finally acknowledged her relationship with Shikhar Pahariya. title: Priyanka Chopra's DIY mehendi for husband Nick Jonas on Karwa Chauth has a special touch for daughter Malti Marie
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Every year, as married Indian women celebrate Karwa Chauth, applying mehendi to their palms becomes an integral part of the festivities. Star Priyanka Chopra continues to embrace her Indian traditions and has now offered a glimpse of her Karwa Chauth celebrations. This year, her DIY mehendi design was not just about her husband, Nick Jonas, but also featured a special tribute to their daughter, Malti Marie Chopra Jonas.

Adding to this, Priyanka Chopra sends Karwa Chauth wishes to followers. Priyanka Chopra's mehendi for Karwa Chauth On Thursday, Priyanka posted on Instagram to share pictures of her mehendi design, which she applied herself. The star incorporated the initials of both Nick and Malti into the design, adding a personal touch to the occasion. Sharing the pictures, she wrote, "DIY..Piya ke naam ki (in the name of my husband).. happy karwachauth to all those celebrating."

Meanwhile, In another picture, she offered a glimpse of herself applying chashni (sugar syrup) to her mehendi and wrote, "The question is will the chashni work? IYKYK." Many Indian women follow this practice to help their mehendi develop a darker colour. Priyanka's celebrations offered a glimpse of how she continues to observe the traditions associated with the festival while living away from India.

Notably, Earlier, during an appearance on The Kapil Sharma Show in 2025, Priyanka recalled a romantic gesture Nick made for her during Karwa Chauth that set relationship goals. She shared, "We’ve tried to spot the moon in the strangest places. Once, we were at a stadium where he was doing a show, and the moon just wouldn’t appear. There were clouds, and rain was about to start. Around 60–70 thousand people were present and the show kept going on. We waited till 10 pm, then 11 pm, and still the moon wasn’t visible."

As per the latest buzz, She added, "Want to hear something romantic? He finally took me up in a plane, above the clouds, and then I broke my fast after seeing the moon." Her revelation left the audience in awe, while followers on the internet could not stop gushing about the romantic gesture.

In further updates, The couple first met at the 2017 Met Gala, where they walked the red carpet together, representing Ralph Lauren. However, their romance blossomed only the following year, when they began dating. Nick proposed to Priyanka in July 2018, on her birthday, and the couple got married in December that year in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, in Christian and Hindu wedding ceremonies.

On top of that, In January 2022, Priyanka and Nick welcomed their daughter, Malti Marie Chopra Jonas, via surrogacy. Malti was born prematurely and spent more than three months in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) before she could go home with her parents.

Priyanka will soon make her comeback to Indian cinema with SS Rajamouli's Varanasi. The movie also stars Mahesh Babu and Prithviraj Sukumaran in lead roles and is shared to be one of the most ambitious projects in Indian cinema, mounted on a massive budget of ₹ 1,000 crore rupees. The movie is scheduled to rollout in theatres in April 2027.

title: Exclusive | Bhumi Pednekkar set to reunite with Akshay Kumar in Priyadarshan's next film

(Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) (AFP) What Sai Pallavi shared In response, Sai shared, “Pehle achche insaan hone chahiye (Firstly he should be a good man). He should not be very self-centred. He should be someone who is introspective. One who checks on his actions. So someone who has some insight about where he is in life… he can make mistakes but he must mend it too. It should not be that he is blaming it on someone else. It is not that there is a huge list but he should be a good person and it would be better if he also knows how to cook!”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sony LIV (@sonylivindia)

Notably, In the episode, Amitabh also asked Sai about her decision to pursue acting after studying medicine. As per the latest buzz, In another promo, Sai opened up about her initial reaction when she was offered the role of Sita in Ramayana. She shared, “I didn’t want to use my head this time. title: Anurag Kashyap made Gangs of Wasseypur sets feel like a playground, never flaunted authority: Short film Aakhiri Ride makers
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Writer-director and VFX supervisors Yashoda Parthasarthy and Vijesh Rajan began their journeys in the movie industry with Anurag Kashyap . While Vijesh was part of the team behind Gangs of Wasseypur , Yashoda worked with the filmmaker on Raman Raghav 20. Their latest short movie, Aakhiri Ride, is also presented by Anurag and Vasan Bala .

Adding to this, Aakhri Ride makers Yashoda Parthasarthy and Vijesh Rajan spoke about starting their careers with Anurag Kashyap. In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, the duo spoke about how Anurag's early influence shaped their understanding of cinema. They also discussed casting Panchayat star Chandan Roy and featuring the voice of fellow Panchayat star Faisal Malik in their short movie, as well as how their observations during long cab rides across Mumbai inspired Aakhiri Ride.

Meanwhile, Yashoda: While writing Scam Raju's (Faisal Malik) character, I could just hear Faizal Bhai's voice. We have a working relationship with him for many years now. When we approached him, he agreed, and he really loved the script as well.

Notably, Chandan's story is quite unique because when I first made my mom read the script, she recommended him, but I didn't believe that an star from Panchayat-like big show will star in my short movie. We had narrated it to a couple of actors, but we felt like something was missing, and also they were not from UP or Bihar. We wanted someone who looks very dedicated to his work and has a little bit of innocence. Later, our casting team also recommended Chandan, and as soon as he came into the meeting room, we were like, 'Wow, he is perfect'. He is so humble, intelligent, and technically very sound. He's also very dedicated; he would often be like, 'Can I say this line again?' He is very layered as a person, which was quite fun to explore during the process.

As per the latest buzz, Vijesh: It was actually also our way to pay homage to Hindi 90s cinema tropes — a truthful hero whose sister is getting married, a 90s plot where the cop comes at the end, a villain who pops up. We wanted to do our own take on that.

In further updates, Vijesh/Yashoda: A lot of drivers come from UP and Bihar to work in metro cities. Yashoda and I often travel long distances across Mumbai by cab, and that's when we started noticing the drivers and hearing about their problems. So, the movie is somewhat based on several real-life incidents.

On top of that, I remember one particular driver who was in a state of panic, making multiple calls. We couldn't fully understand what he was saying because of the dialect, but he clearly needed to arrange money urgently. Yashoda and I spoke about the tragedy of that situation — both of us sitting comfortably in the back seat, being driven home by someone who might not even have a home to go to, someone who was struggling to make ends meet and suddenly had to arrange money for a payment. That became our starting point for figuring out how to tell this story.

Yashoda: Personally, what I learned from him is that he encourages you to have your own voice. He has a strong creative vision, but he gives you the space to bring your own perspective. He is not selfish. He believes the industry needs to grow. If there are 20 good filmmakers, there will be 20 great films, more opportunities, and audiences will have better choices. We will spoil everyone. Making space for other artists is his philosophy, and I love it.

title: Janhvi Kapoor says she should have been more vigilant about the objectification in Peddi, admits the role propagated sexual assualt in the narrative
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Buchi Babu Sana's sports action drama, Peddi, rolled out in theatres on June 4. The movie faced criticism from a section of viewers over the hypersexualisation of Janhvi Kapoor 's character. Later, director Buchi Babu Sana took to X (formerly Twitter) to issue an apology for the star’s portrayal in the movie and changes were made. Now, months later, Janhvi has opened up about the entire backlash surrounding the movie and her character during her appearance on the chat show Koffee with Karan .

Adding to this, Janhvi Kapoor in a still from Peddi. What Janhvi shared When host Karan Johar asked her about how she processed the entire issue, Janhvi shared, “I feel many people worked really hard on that movie and I really didn't know if there was anything to say. It weighs heavily on my conscience the sort of negative impact a narrative like that can have our society. Specific to my gender. That shame I will always carry with me. Could I have done more? Could I have been more vigilant? 100% yes. Was it problematic, was it extreme objectification? Did it even propagate sexual assault narratively? Yes. But the only thing I can do is ensure that it doesn't happen again.”

Meanwhile, She went on to add, “I went through the beats of really beating up myself that I should have been more vigilant. I don't like saying this because it sounds like i am shifting blame but its like you listen to the director and what he says. I was navigating how to make things less problematic as and when information was becoming available to me. In the south, very rarely there is a bound script. very rarely do u see the camera angles. I should have taken advantage of my privilege. It was a violating experience in a way. the good thing that came out of it is that maybe next time a director will rethink twice before presenting a lead star this way.”

Notably, Peddi is a sports drama in which Ram plays the titular character. Janhvi plays Achiyamma, Peddi’s love interest. Since the movie's rollout, viewers have criticised the way Janhvi's character, Achiyyamma, is introduced on screen. Many pointed to sequences that focus heavily on her body rather than establishing her as a character. Another scene that came under scrutiny involves Peddi expressing his desire to be with Achiyyamma despite her lack of interest and later kissing her during a power cut without her consent.

As per the latest buzz, Following the backlash, director Buchi Babu Sana issued an apology on X and acknowledged the concerns raised by audiences. A part of his statement read, "I have always had immense respect for women, both on and off screen, and it was never our intention to objectify or disrespect any female character. If any part of the movie has been perceived that way, we respect those sentiments, understand the concerns being raised, and sincerely apologise. After reviewing the feedback, we have decided to make changes to the concerned portions."

title: Could Yash’s Ravana steal the thunder from Ranbir Kapoor’s Lord Ram? The STAR POWER battle inside Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

But beyond its scale and technological ambition, the movie presents a fascinating star-power experiment. Can Yash, who became a pan-Indian phenomenon through KGF , attract as much attention as Ranbir Kapoor, the star playing the central protagonist?

Adding to this, The question isn’t about which character is more important to the story. Lord Rama is the moral and narrative centre of the epic, while Ravana represents its formidable opposition. Rather, it concerns an interesting phenomenon in commercial cinema. Audiences are often fascinated by a larger-than-life antagonist.

Meanwhile, Hindi cinema has a long history of memorable villains. Gabbar Singh, Mogambo and several other iconic antagonists continue to occupy an extraordinary place in popular culture. In more recent years, major action films have relied increasingly on powerful adversaries whose personalities, appearances and dramatic entrances become central attractions. Yash’s casting brings another dimension to this tradition.

Notably, Through KGF , the Kannada superstar demonstrated that an star could transcend linguistic boundaries and become popular across the country. Rocky Bhai’s appeal rested on his attitude, dialogue delivery, visual presentation and larger-than-life personality. Now Yash is stepping into an altogether different universe.

As per the latest buzz, Ravana is not a conventional action-movie villain. He is a complex mythological figure traditionally depicted as immensely powerful, knowledgeable and accomplished, but ultimately brought down by his own choices. For Yash, this offers an opportunity to create a character that combines physical presence with dramatic complexity.

In further updates, In that sense, Ramayana represents two contrasting forms of stardom. Yash’s existing mass appeal could be well suited to Ravana’s imposing personality. Ranbir’s strength as an star lies in his ability to communicate vulnerability, internal conflict and emotion. If the movie is successful, audiences could be drawn to both for different reasons.

On top of that, There is also the geographical dimension. Ranbir is an established Hindi movie star with major domestic successes, including Sanju , Brahmastra and Animal . Yash, on the other hand, enjoys an especially strong identity in the Kannada market and has demonstrated considerable appeal beyond it.
By bringing them together, the makers have created an opportunity to attract Hindi speaking viewers, South Indian audiences and overseas moviegoers through a single project.

According to a statement issued by Saffron Magicworks, the court set aside the impugned award passed by IMPPA’s Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC), with the court recording that the suit stood disposed of and nothing further survived for consideration in the pending applications.

Adding to this, The development follows an interim order dated September 9, 2026, passed by Justice Arif S Doctor, under which the court had restrained IMPPA from declaring Saffron Magicworks a defaulter consequent to the disputed award until further orders.
Meanwhile, The September order had also recorded a statement made on instructions by counsel for Defendant No. 2 that the party would not act upon the impugned award.

Notably, Saffron Magicworks had approached the High Court challenging the award passed through IMPPA’s dispute resolution mechanism and seeking protection against its implementation and the consequences that could follow from it.

As per the latest buzz, In its latest order dated October 23, 2026, Justice Arif S Doctor specifically addressed IMPPA’s position, observing that since the association’s own committee had passed the purported award, IMPPA could not be aggrieved by its setting aside.
In further updates, The latest development assumes significance against the backdrop of the disagreement between the parties over the interpretation of the court’s earlier directions.

On top of that, Saffron Magicworks has alleged that IMPPA’s public statement on the proceedings was materially misleading on the central question of whether the association had been restrained by the court. The production house’s position was that the September 9 order expressly prohibited IMPPA from declaring it a defaulter on the basis of the July 3 award.
The production house further maintained that any suggestion that the court had imposed no such restraint was inconsistent with the wording of paragraph four of the order.

title: Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra calls Los Angeles premiere his “Oscar moment” ahead of November 5 release
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
“I wanted to host this evening at the Academy Theatre because this is my Oscar moment,” Malhotra shared during his address.

Adding to this, Malhotra also spoke about his association with Los Angeles and his work in visual effects through DNEG. He noted that the company has won eight Academy Awards, including seven over the past 11 years, for its collaborations with filmmakers such as Christopher Nolan and Denis Villeneuve.

Meanwhile, Reflecting on his beginnings, he shared, “For a third generation movie family background, garage startup kid at 19 with an Apple computer working with three of his teachers who are all of 21, Merzin, Prakash and Josefa, this is what dreams are made of and what better place to share this moment than the city of Angels, Los Angeles.”

Notably, Malhotra also recalled moving to Los Angeles in 2007 as part of his efforts to build a company that could connect Indian and international movie industries. “In my pursuit of building a global company and connecting the east and the west I set foot in LA in 2007 and haven't looked back since,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, He further spoke about the financial difficulties he faced during the 2008 crisis and how the experience shaped his journey. “An immigrant who lost 90% of his wealth with the fun times in 2008 as I'm sure some of you may remember to bounce back today and being able to bring the biggest independent production in the world the Ramayana, I can't even tell you what it feels like to stand here today,” he shared.

In further updates, During his address, Malhotra brought the movie's key collaborators on stage. He introduced Nitesh Tiwari as the director, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram and Sai Pallavi as Sita. “As you all can see Ram without Sita does not work. So please welcome Sai Pallavi,” he shared.

On top of that, He then introduced Yash, who plays Ravana in the movie, saying, “And the reason that you know this movie happened or the conflict happened is because they have to fight Raavan, and that is the rocking star Yash.” Malhotra also acknowledged the contribution of international and Indian talent involved in the project, including composer Hans Zimmer and choreographer Terry Notary.

Speaking about the larger vision behind Ramayana , Malhotra shared the movie brought together talent from both India and the West. “I stand here to showcase the best of India and the best of the west working together to create a motion picture that means more to billions of people around the world than you all can imagine,” he shared.

title: ‘Ravana is not all bad’: Sai Pallavi says key takeaway from Ramayana is to spot the Ravana in us and make changes over time
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

All eyes are on Ramayana as it gears up for rollout in a few days. Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi , Yash and director Nitesh Tiwari attended the Los Angeles premiere of Ramayana at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. On the red carpet, Sai Pallavi spoke about the movie and shared what she hopes that audience takes away from the movie adaptation of the Indian epic.

Adding to this, Sai Pallavi has spoken about the portrayal of Ravana in Ramayana. What Sai Pallavi shared Sai Pallavi was asked that people in India have grown up with the story of Ramayana but what does she hope the people see differently in the movie in US. In response, Sai shared, “If one is curious about Indian culture, Indian epics, I think this could be the start where you see the best version of Ramayana that exists.” She shared that the movie has the best technicians on board along with advanced VFX.

Meanwhile, She went on to add, “At the same time, as a scripture, I think, if you are a believer, and you would see, try to introspect, and see what good and bad exists in you, and you learn to correct yourself over time. Because Ravana is not all bad. And it's important that we spot the Ravana in us, and we make changes over time.”

Notably, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita and Yash plays Ravana. The cast also includes Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

As per the latest buzz, As per reports mounted on a budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees, the movie is backed by Yash and Namit Malhotra and is planned as a two-part franchise. The first instalment is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 5, 2026, with the second part expected to arrive around Diwali 2027.

title: Manoj Bajpayee recalls career low before Raajneeti, Gangs Of Wasseypur; says meetings with Neeraj Pandey, Anurag Kashyap changed everything
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Manoj Bajpayee has opened up about a low phase in his career before films such as Raajneeti, Gangs Of Wasseypur and Special 26 brought a significant change. The star recalled a time when he was turning down several offers because the kind of work he wanted to do was not coming his way. He also spoke about how conversations with filmmakers Prakash Jha, director of Raajneeti, Anurag Kashyap , director of Gangs Of Wasseypur, and Neeraj Pandey, eventually led to these films.

Adding to this, Manoj Bajpayee latest movie Gajab Raat is streaming on Netflix. Manoj Bajpayee on the low phase in his career Recalling that period, Manoj shared, “Before these films, I saw some lows. The kind of work that I wanted to do wasn’t coming my way. All I was doing was refusing films and saying no to people. And the ones I shared yes to, I wasn’t happy doing those films."

Meanwhile, The star explained that things began to change after he watched Neeraj Pandey's A Wednesday. He met the filmmaker afterwards. Around the same time, he also met Prakash Jha and was in touch with Anurag Kashyap.

Notably, Talking about how these meetings eventually led to new opportunities, Manoj shared, “That’s when I watched A Wednesday. Neeraj (Pandey) and I had met after that and we spoke about cinema at large. He told me how he makes his films. That’s all I remember from that chat. I also remember meeting Prakash (Jha) ji at around the same time. Anurag (Kashyap) and I were talking simultaneously. Those films started happening to me a year after those meetings."

As per the latest buzz, Manoj went on to share that he continues to speak to directors every day, including many newcomers. He shared these conversations help him discover interesting stories and find the kind of work he wants to do. The star added that his focus is on building a filmography that he can be proud of.

In further updates, Manoj was of late seen in Gajab Raat, which premiered on Netflix on October 23. title: Radhika Apte slams trolls criticising Alia Bhatt's physique in Alpha, calls out double standards for female actors in action roles
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Alia Bhatt 's latest rollout, Alpha , faced criticism and eventually failed at the ticket-window. The star was seen in an action-packed avatar in the movie. However, many viewers criticised her for lacking the physicality required for an action role. In a recent interview with India Today, Radhika Apte questioned why female actors are scrutinised for their physique when taking on action roles, while their male counterparts rarely face the same judgement.

Adding to this, Radhika Apte slams trolls criticising Alia Bhatt's action sequences in Alpha. Radhika Apte defends Alia Bhatt Radhika and Keerthy Suresh are set to star in the crime thriller series Akka. When asked about the audience's hesitation towards female actors leading crime dramas, the two actors shared they believed things were changing, citing examples such as Samantha Ruth Prabhu's performance in The Family Man and Kalyani Priyadarshan's role in Lokah. When they were told that Alia had been trolled for not fitting the part of an action hero in Alpha, Radhika hit back at the trolls, saying, "Your actors who are doing action have massive paunches and all, and Alia is bloody fit. I mean, please."

Meanwhile, Further explaining why these double standards exist, Radhika shared, "I think it's because most households and a large part of our country are quite traditional. You want women to be a certain way, dress a certain way, behave a certain way, and get married at a certain age. That still exists. Very few people are comfortable with the freedom that their daughters are seeking, or rather, rightfully claiming. I think that also reflects in the kind of content people watch. That's my guess."

Notably, Alia faced criticism for her role in Alpha, with social media users questioning her casting as an 18-year-old character despite being in her 30s. Her action avatar subsequently attracted criticism over her physique. The movie, directed by Shiv Rawail, also faced criticism for its storyline and dialogues. Featuring Anil Kapoor, Bobby Deol and Sharvari in key roles alongside Alia, the movie collected only ₹ 99 crore rupees worldwide at the ticket-window.

title: Jamia alleges campus vandalism amid protests, says university gates, CCTV cameras damaged
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Jamia Millia Islamia on Wednesday alleged widespread vandalism on its campus through Tuesday night, claiming that groups of protesting students and locals damaged university gates and boundary walls, brought down Gate 4C, threw stones, and damaged CCTV cameras and their control room amid an ongoing protest.

Adding to this, The allegations came amid protests against the university administration’s decision to restrict access to the campus. (PTI) In a statement on Wednesday, the university shared the incidents raised serious concerns about the safety of students, faculty members and non-teaching staff. It alleged that a group of masked protesters reached the university’s boys’ hostels to mobilise additional support.

Meanwhile, The allegations came amid protests against the university administration’s decision to restrict access to the campus, with hostel residents particularly angered by the closure of Gate 4C, which they use to enter the university.

Notably, A protesting student, not wishing to be identified, shared, “The university administration had sealed Gate 4C, which is used by hostel students to reach the university campus. There are two halls - Zakir Hussain Hall and Jauhar Hall -- that house eight hostels. Residents of these hostels were angry about the administration’s decision to close the entry. They broke the gate to gain entry to the campus.” He shared they will chalk out the further course of action on Wednesday.

As per the latest buzz, The university shared its proctorial team and teachers rushed to the campus after receiving reports of the attacks. It alleged that the scale and intensity of the damage were particularly concerning, with videos, CCTV footage and social media posts indicating that heavy iron rods, hammers and other tools had been used to damage university infrastructure.

In further updates, The administration alleged that women faculty members, wardens and provosts were threatened when they attempted to reason with female protesters. It shared the vandalism began shortly after another attempt by the university to hold dialogue with the protesting students.

On top of that, The statement shared the university administration had made seven attempts to engage with the protesters, including negotiations with committee members and teachers on Tuesday evening. The university expressed dismay at what it described as a contradiction between the students’ participation in discussions and the destruction that followed.

The incidents, it shared, came after a week of repeated instances of university gates and boundary walls being scaled, damaged and broken. The university has shifted to online mode, as notified on October 24.

title: Radhika Apte talks about avoiding South films, says fair-skinned North Indian female actors were favoured over local talent
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In her two-decade-long career, Radhika Apte has been part of several South Indian films, including Vetri Selvan, Rajinikanth’s Kabali and Lion. Her last South Indian movie was Chithiram Pesuthadi 2 (2019), which rolled out six years after she shot for it. In a recent interaction, Radhika opened up about why she has consciously kept away from South Indian cinema, saying she felt the industry had a bias towards fair-skinned female actors.

Adding to this, Radhika Apte is currently busy with the promotions of her next movie Akka. 'North Indian female actors were cast down south because they were fairer' In conversation with News18, Radhika shared, “I could be wrong but in my perception, north Indian actresses were cast down south because they were fairer. I’m not fair. I wonder, why they wouldn’t cast south Indian actresses in south Indian films and get north Indian actresses instead. And here, they want foreigners. We’ve a tendency to do that. I didn’t want to promote that. Women down south are absolutely beautiful, talented and amazing, who know the language really well. They’re excellent performers. I think they should get cast in south films rather than people coming from Bombay, who can’t speak a word in that language and get their voices dubbed by others. I wasn’t very much in favour of all that.”

Meanwhile, Radhika also shared that the atmosphere on South Indian movie sets was informal, which could have both advantages and disadvantages. She shared, “I did my last south movie ten years back. And what I recollect is that things were a bit more informal there. A lot of things happened out of dosti. They were very soft and kind. They would tell me, ‘You’re like family now.’ They treated you as though you were their sister. But that would mean that I would also have to do things out of favour. That would become a problem. But it was also nice because you felt you could go and chat with them.”

Notably, Radhika will next be seen in Akka, a Netflix gangster drama set in the 1980s in the fictional South Indian kingdom of Pernuru. She plays Rudra, who finds herself in a power struggle with Bhavani, played by Keerthy Suresh.

As per the latest buzz, Written and directed by Dharmaraj Shetty and produced by YRF Entertainment, the series explores power, loyalty, rivalry and revenge. Akka is set to premiere on Netflix on October 30, 2026.

title: Govinda recalls mother's struggles after she became a heroine, reveals why she shaved her head and became a Sadhvi
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Govinda has often spoken about sharing a close bond with his late mother, Nirmala Devi. In a recent interview with ABP Live, Govinda spoke about his mother's sacrifices, recalling why she gave up her acting career and became a spiritual ascetic.

Adding to this, Govinda opens up about his mother's struggles. Govinda talks about her mother's sacrifice Nirmala Devi began her career as a leading star in Hindi cinema but stepped away from the industry after less than a decade. Govinda recalled, "After becoming a heroine, my mother Nirmala Devi got poor to such an extent that all the stuff from our bungalow was taken away."

Meanwhile, Explaining why his mother became a sadhvi, Govinda shared, "My father told her, ‘Nirmala, you’re so pretty that when you go out to ask for work, people would ogle at you.’ So my poor mother got her shaved off and became a saint. She shared, ‘Let my children grow up'. Being the son of such a mother, I don’t care about who’s saying what about me. I’m not even looking in that direction."

Notably, Govinda also opened up that his mother never wanted him to become a hero. Recalling how she reacted when he expressed his desire to become an star, he shared she felt he was too innocent for the demands of the entertainment industry. She also did not want him to smoke or drink alcohol. Govinda opened up that his mother wanted him to take up a bank job, while his father believed in his potential.

As per the latest buzz, Nirmala Devi was an star and Hindustani classical vocalist who began her movie career in the early 1940s. She made her acting debut with Savera (1942), directed by V C Desai, in which she starred alongside Arun Kumar Ahuja, whom she married in the same year. She went on to appear in films such as Sharda (1942), Kanoon (1943), Geet (1944), Gaali (1944) and Piya Milan (1945). Her performance in Chalis Karod (1946) also received positive reviews.

In further updates, She later featured in Ghunghat (1946) and Sehra (1948), a home production made by her husband. She continued acting in films such as Anmol Ratan (1950) and Jai Mahalakshmi (1951), which marked her final screen appearance. Although she stepped away from acting relatively early, she continued pursuing music and established herself as a Hindustani classical vocalist known for her thumri performances.

title: Katrina Kaif says Vicky Kaushal is 100% present with son Vihaan even after 18-hour workdays, reveals their romantic dinners have taken a backseat
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Vicky Kaushal and Katrina Kaif became parents last year. Although the couple have kept their personal lives away from the cameras, including keeping their son Vihaan Kaushal out of the public eye, they occasionally open up about their family life. In a recent interaction, Katrina showered praise on her husband, star Vicky, and called him an “amazing” father.

Adding to this, Katrina Kaif lauded Vicky Kaushal for being an amazing father. 'Vicky is wise in practice, I am wise in theory' In conversation with Vogue, Katrina lauded Vicky for being patient and a good listener, describing him as the perfect partner for someone like her, who tends to have a lot to say. She shared, "Vicky is an incredible husband. He is wise beyond his years, has strong family values and a true sense of integrity. I would say Vicky is wise in practice, and I am wise in theory. One of the best things about him is that he always gives me space to be myself while being a great listener, and I can have a lot to say sometimes.”

Meanwhile, Katrina also lauded Vicky's ability to be fully present with her and their son despite his hectic work schedule. However, she admitted that balancing their high-profile careers and parenthood has meant fewer romantic dinners and movie nights.

Notably, “As a father, he’s been amazing. He has this incredible superpower to be 100 per cent present in the moment with Vihaan and me, even when he is tired and has been working 14, 16 or 18 hours a day. Our romantic dinners and movie nights have taken a backseat for now, but Vicky keeps reminding me that everything will find its own time again,” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Since becoming a mother, Katrina has largely stayed away from the spotlight. However, the star was of late spotted at Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations and out and about in Mumbai. She has also faced body-shaming comments following the birth of her son.

In further updates, Of late, at an event in London, Katrina responded to online trolls and spoke about the importance of not letting social media criticism affect one's self-worth. She shared, “I think we really need to be careful in letting the narrative on social media affect our self-worth. If we start trying to cater to all of them, I think that really hampers your ability to make choices for yourself. Personally, if every time I face critique or comments, I let that dictate my actions, I think I would have been paralysed with fear and unable to move ahead in my life.”

On top of that, Katrina has been selective about her movie roles since marrying Vicky in 2021. The couple welcomed their son in 2025. In addition to her acting career, Katrina has focused on expanding her makeup brand, Kay Beauty, which of late launched in the UK. On the movie front, she was last seen in the 2024 movie Merry Christmas, directed by Sriram Raghavan and co-starring Vijay Sethupathi.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Moreover, the poster mentions 'Filmed for IMAX', hinting that the movie will also get an IMAX rollout in the country. However, the exact rollout date is yet to be revealed. The poster simply mentions 'Only in theatres this November'.
Adding to this, A post shared by PVRINOX Pictures (@pvrpictures)

Ramayana is a local movie and has a two-week exclusivity window on IMAX screens in India. This means that at most IMAX cinemas, it is likely to get just one show, while the remaining shows will be allotted to Ramayana .
