title: Anti-SIR protest LIVE: SEM hands over documents cited by Delhi Police in show-cause notice issued to Neha Bora
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

All India Students' Association (AISA) National President Neha Bora addresses a press conference at the CPI(ML) Liberation Parliamentary Office, in New Delhi on Thursday. Anti-SIR protest highlights: AISA's Neha Bora on Saturday shared they would not sign a peace bond, while terming the evidence against them as “factually incorrect.” This came a day after Delhi High Court dismissed their plea challenging a police notice which directed them to execute e a ₹ 10,000 personal bond with the surety to maintain peace. ...Read More

Adding to this, Bora disputed the evidence presented by the cops, while claiming that the Central Park protest, which was cited in the police notice as evidence, was not called by AISA. “One of the grounds for making us sign a peace bond – in the notice it is written that we went to CP and protested which breaches peace. The clarification is that Central Park call was not given by us. So the evidence is factually incorrect,” Bora told reporters on Saturday. Bora further questioned what constituted as “breach of peace”, while citing alleged voter deletions through the special intensive revision exercise. “Next question is - when you talk about peace, who are you asking peace for? In the country, 13 crore rupees voters have been removed from the voters list. When in the system, common people are being disenfranchised, peaceful protest is the way through which they can question the government. Is raising this question breach of peace? Not questioning the government is peace?” Bora asked. CJP launches criticism against CEC CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka on Saturday shared no bond could stop people from protesting. “No bond bars our constitutional right to protest, unless of course Paw-Paw is planning to change the Constitution,” Ranka shared in a post on X. This came even as CJP co-convener Saurav Das launched a fresh attack on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, claiming his “days are numbered.” “Unfortunately, the most dishonourable men are in positions of power in our country today. But. Their time is up,” Das shared in a post on X, even as CJP leaders vowed to continue their movement against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Das and Ranka were detained following an incident on October 12, when they scaled a gate and entered Jantar Mantar, a day after it was de-notified as a protest site. After spending a week in judicial custody, the two leaders were granted relief on October 21 after furnishing personal and surety bonds of ₹ 50,000 each. They submitted written undertakings committing to maintain peace and public tranquility and not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the area is officially re-notified as a designated protest site. Das and Ranka appeared at the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court at Delhi's Mandir Marg Police Station on Friday afternoon after being asked by the court to appear in person with their sureties while being rolled out in the earlier hearing. Yogendra Yadav's ‘human chain’ call Activist Yogendra Yadav has called for a “human chain” in Hyderabad's Tank Bund on Saturday. “Hyderabad, join the human chain at Tank Bund this Saturday, 4 PM, with the national flag to stand against vote chori and defend electoral democracy,” Yadav shared in a post on X. He added, “Let’s raise our voices for free and fair elections!” Why is CEC Gyanesh Kumar under fire? The demonstrations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar flared after an investigative report by The Indian Express that claimed Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months regarding decisions taken by the poll body. These included those linked to the SIR. The Election Commission has rejected these allegations, saying that major decisions, including the SIR of electoral rolls, had been taken unanimously by the full commission. Delhi HC rejects Neha Bora's plea against signing peace bond Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court rejected a plea by All India Students' Association president Neha Bora, challenging a police notice asking them to execute a peace bond. The HC held that there was sufficient material before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) to take such action against them. Justice Subramonium Prasad shared the notice met the requirement of law and was “not based merely on hearsay material.”

Meanwhile, Anti-SIR protest LIVE: All India Students' Association (AISA) National President Neha Bora on Saturday appeared before the SEM Court at Mandir Marg Police Station after the Delhi High Court dismissed Bora’s plea yesterday, challenging the court notice asking them to execute a ₹ 10,000 bond with a surety to maintain peace during the inquiry.

Notably, During the court proceedings, the SEM Court asked the police to give the documents to Neha Bora's counsel. The Special Executive Magistrate granted time to the counsel to file a reply. The matter has been scheduled for further hearing on October 29.

As per the latest buzz, Advocate Abhik Chimni, representing Neha Bora, shared that the legal team will analyse all the documents received today and will proceed accordingly. He underlined that anyone who is detained has a right to know what is held against them. They must also have a reasonable opportunity to respond.

In further updates, "We approached the High Court challenging the show cause notice Neha Bora received. The High Court has dismissed the challenge to the show cause notice. The High Court has laid down certain parameters and tests. One of them was that, in paragraph 38 of the judgment, the High Court has shared that all the material that was relied upon to state that there may be a breach of peace, and all the underlying material relied upon by the SEM, may be provided to us. Today we showed the SEM the judgment, and he has been kind enough to give us all the documents. We will now proceed and see those documents. The next date is on the 29th. The findings in paras 38 and 50, etc., have helped develop the criminal code to ensure that when anybody is detained, they have a right to know what is held against them and they have a reasoned opportunity to reply," she shared.
On top of that, “No bond bars our constitutional right to protest, unless ofcourse Paw-Paw is planning to change the Constitution,” Ranka shared.

Anti-SIR protest LIVE: AISA president Neha Bora appeared before the special executive magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg Police Station on Saturday, a day after the Delhi High Court dismissed her plea challenging a police notice directing her to execute a ₹ 10,000 "peace bond" with one surety.

title: Manoj Bajpayee says he felt offended, helpless when 'faceless, nameless' trolls attacked his wife and daughter over Ghooskhor Pandat row
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Manoj Bajpayee has shared that he has developed a thick skin when it comes to criticism but he did get concerned and offended when people began dragging his family into the row surrounding the previous title of his movie, Gajab Raat.

Adding to this, Manoj Bajpayee in a still from Netflix's Gajab Raat, which resulted in FIRs and backlash. Manoj Bajpayee recalls trolling for Ghooskhor Pandat The Netflix movie, directed by Ritesh Shah, was originally revealed by Netflix in February this year as Ghooskhor Pandat . The title triggered a social media backlash with several politicians and organisations calling it "casteist and offensive". The makers later changed the title.

Meanwhile, But the makers and Manoj received a lot of online hate following the row. In a recent interview with PTI, Manoj recalled the time, saying, “You go ahead and assault me with the worst thing, I'll take it because I'm an star. I've had a journey from rejection to everything (where) you are called all sorts of things. So you are thick-skinned. At the end of the day, I feel bad all those people, who are either very ignorant or have less knowledge about life. What really concerned me and offended me to no bits is when they started publishing the photo(s) of my family and saying things.”

Notably, Manoj is married to star Shabana Raza, who appeared in films like Kareeb and Fiza. They have a daughter together. He recalled that the abuse faced by his family was from ‘nameless’ trolls, which meant he could not confront them.

As per the latest buzz, “I am a person who is very easy (going) in life, I like to be happy and have fun all the time. But at the same time, when there is an urgency to save my near and dear ones, I'm very confrontational... But who could I confront because there are nameless people out there,” the star shared.
In further updates, Eventually, the movie was retitled Gajab Raat, with the first teaser releasing earlier this month. The movie rolled out on Netflix this Friday, October 23.

On top of that, Directed by Ritesh Shah and produced by Neeraj Pandey 's Friday Storytellers, Gajab Raat follows Ajay Nirvit, a cop whose act of compassion towards an injured woman draws him into a high-level conspiracy and a deadly game that unfolds over a single night.
Gajab Raat also stars Divya Dutta, Saqib Saleem, Shraddha Das, and Akshay Oberoi, with Kiku Sharda and Nushrratt Bharuccha in special appearances. The movie us currently streaming on Netflix.

title: Radhika Apte says most women in Bollywood have to do films led by men as only Alia Bhatt or Deepika Padukone can get theatrical opening
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Radhika Apte says female stars in Hindi cinema are almost compelled to appear in male-led films when it comes to theatrical releases because the uncertainty surrounding ticket-window makes it difficult for female-led films to secure a strong theatrical rollout. The star added that the only way a female-led movie can even secure a good box-office opening is if it is headlined by top stars like Alia Bhatt or Deepika Padukone.

Adding to this, Radhika Apte believes only top stars like Alia and Deepika can guarantee a box-office opening in India. Radhika Apte on female-led films Radhika, who is currently promoting her soon-to-release Netflix web series, Akka, has seen all of her last few films - Lust Stories 3, Saali Mohabbat, Mrs Undercover, and Monica, O My Darling - rollout directly on streaming. However, Radhika says she did not choose projects based on the medium.

Meanwhile, “I don't take a project based on whether it's theatrical or OTT. I don't really care about it. There are so many business decisions dependent on that; I'd rather be like 'let the movie come out one way or another',” the star told PTI in an interview.

Notably, Radhika added that female actors take up films where men are doing the lead roles due to box-office consideration. “With theatrical releases in the last few years we don't know what is working or what isn't. A theatrical rollout where I am the lead would probably tank even if it's the best movie. I don't have that, like generally, I'm not an Alia Bhatt or Deepika Padukone where you can, at least, hope that they'll be opening. I'm being very honest with you. That means I have to be in a movie where men are doing the main part,” Radhika shared.

As per the latest buzz, Despite Radhika's confidence in Alia and Deepika, the two stars haven't given a big box-office solo hit in a while. Alia did star in Gangubai Kathiawadi, which remains one of the highest-grossing female-led films in Hindi cinema, in 2022. But her subsequent solo releases - Jigra and Alpha - tanked at the ticket-window. Deepika has not appeared in a solo theatrical rollout since her 2018 rollout Chhapaak.

In further updates, The two actors have starred in big films led by other actors, which have gone on to be big blockbusters. Alia was part of Brahmastra and RRR, both of which did well at the ticket-window. In Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani, her last box-office success, she shared the spoils with Ranveer Singh.

title: Interview | Sourav Ganguly’s iconic 2002 shirt-waving celebration on Lord’s balcony inspired Abhinay Deo's Doosra
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sourav Ganguly ’s shirt-waving celebration at Lord’s in 2002 is still remembered as one of Indian cricket’s most defiant moments. After India beat England in the NatWest Series final, the Indian captain took off his shirt and waved it from the balcony, giving the victory a memorable edge. For filmmaker Abhinay Deo , the moment was about refusing to be treated as inferior, an idea that now forms the backbone of his movie Doosra .

Adding to this, ‘Freedom from inferiority and subservience’: Abhinay Deo on Sourav Ganguly’s influence and his movie Doosra. Interestingly, Sourav Ganguly moved court to stay the rollout of the movie Doosra on October 23. He filed the case over a violation of his 'personality rights'. As per the latest update from Bar and Bench, the Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to stay the rollout of the movie Doosra in a suit field by former Indian cricket captain.

Meanwhile, The movie, which rolled out on October 23, follows Tara, played by Plabita Borthakur , a young woman growing up in a conservative household in Rajasthan. Watching Sourav stand his ground makes her question the restrictions she has accepted for years. While cricket sets the story in motion, Abhinay says the movie is really about finding the courage to live without constantly seeking approval from others. Doosra is scheduled to rollout in theatres on October 23.

Notably, In an interview with Hindustan Times, he says, “As an idea, we believe that this is the second freedom struggle of our country. The first one in 1947 is obvious. This is a story of emotional freedom, freedom from inferiority and freedom from subservience,” he says. Explaining why he sees the story as a struggle for personal rather than political freedom, he adds, “I’m not talking about politics at all. I’m talking about the attitude with which the country has shown the world that we are here, and we are here to stay. We are actually good. We’re very good, if not better. We are as good.”

As per the latest buzz, The title Doosra comes from cricket, where the delivery is designed to turn in an unexpected direction. In the movie, that idea takes on a different meaning as Tara starts looking at her life through a new lens. Sourav's defiance makes her realise that she does not have to follow every rule simply because her family or society expects her to.

In further updates, For Abhinay, the former India captain’s attitude was more important than the match itself. He wanted to explore how one person’s refusal to give in could change the way someone else sees the world. “He has been doing that pretty much from the first day of his captaincy. That is the basis of this movie: a person, a personality and an attitude that become an inspiration for this girl. She sees the rebellious side of this man, who unabashedly refuses to take drinks onto the ground. He doesn’t mind getting sidelined for five years by the team or the board, but he still sticks to his decision,” he adds.

On top of that, Tara begins to see Sourav Ganguly’s stubbornness as something she can learn from. His example gives her the confidence to push back against the expectations that have shaped her life. He says, “That idea of dadagiri becomes a mantra for her. She thinks, if he can get away with it, so can I. I think that is a really interesting angle.”

Plabita Borthakur, however, did not grow up watching cricket. To prepare for the role, she watched matches, including the NatWest final, and went through the cricketer's interviews. But she approached the exercise as a way of understanding what Tara sees in him, rather than simply learning about the sport.

title: 57 FIRs filed in October in Delhi over anti-CEC protests; Crime Branch to probe cases
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police have registered 57 first information reports (FIRs) over protests in the Capital demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner ( CEC ) Gyanesh Kumar during October, with all the cases transferred to the Crime Branch for investigation, officials aware of the matter shared on Friday.

Adding to this, Of the 57 FIRs, over 10 mention assault on police personnel, while a majority mention violations of group gathering curbs under Section 163 of the BNSS. (ANI) The transfer follows a decision by senior police officers that all protest-related cases would be investigated by specialised units rather than district police, HT has learnt.

Meanwhile, Crime Branch officers, who sought to remain anonymous, shared they had started receiving case files and technical evidence relating to protests held in central Delhi between October 2 and 23. The branch has also begun analysing footage recorded by body cameras worn by Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel during the demonstrations.

Notably, Of the 57 FIRs, over 10 mention assault on police personnel, while a majority mention violations of group gathering curbs under Section 163 of the BNSS. At least 10 FIRs name political leaders, with Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra named in three FIRs.

As per the latest buzz, Most of the FIRs have been registered against unidentified people, an officer shared, requesting anonymity. However, the cases also name several political and student activists, including Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) convenors Abhijeet Dipke , Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, and student activist Neha Bora, the officer shared.
In further updates, Police will soon begin questioning people involved in planning the protests, officers shared.

On top of that, The cases invoke various offences, including rioting, assault on security personnel, defacement of public property, vandalism, spreading false information, provisions of the Information Technology Act and violation of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Most FIRs were registered on complaints by security personnel, police shared.

The cases include one filed by Delhi Police ACP Vivek Bhagat, who accused a woman journalist of defamation and obstructing a public servant in the discharge of duty, and invoked the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The ACP’s complaint came after the journalist filed a complaint against him alleging sexual harassment, but no FIR has been registered on her complaint. The matter is also being investigated by the Crime Branch.

title: Delhi HC seeks response from the makers of film Doosra on plea by cricketer Sourav Ganguly alleging violation of his personality rights
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sourav Ganguly has moved to court to stay the rollout of the soon-to-release movie Doosra on October 23. He filed the case over a violation of his ‘personality rights’ but the Delhi HC refused to stay the rollout of the movie. As per the latest update on news agency PTI, the Delhi High Court on Friday asked the makers of the movie Doosra to respond to cricketer Sourav Ganguly's plea alleging violation of his personality rights in the movie.

Adding to this, Cricket Association of Bengal President Sourav Ganguly's plea had alleged unauthorised commercial use of his personality. (PTI Photo)(PTI09_18_2026_000153B) (PTI) What did the Court say? A vacation bench of Justice Vinod Kumar shared the issue of any interim relief against the movie can only be decided after the defendants file their replies and asked them to also arrange a screening of the movie, which was rolled out in theatres earlier on Friday.

Meanwhile, Justice Kumar, who held the court while the high court is shut for Dussehra break, issued summons to the movie's producers, director and distributor in the lawsuit by Ganguly and Luv Films LLP, which is producing a biopic of the former cricket captain.

Notably, The senior counsel for the defendants asserted that "Doosra" was not a biopic but a fictional story of a middle-class Rajasthani girl who is inspired by certain sporting events involving the cricketer. "(The defendants to make) arrangements for playing the movie so that it can be decided whether the personality rights of the plaintiff are violated or not," the court shared, as it listed the case for hearing on October 29.

As per the latest buzz, While the defendants' counsel submitted that the plea for an interim relief was infructuous at this stage as the movie had been rolled out, the plaintiffs' lawyer argued that a stay can still be granted.

In further updates, On Thursday, the high court refused to stop the theatre rollout of the movie Doosra on Ganguly's plea. The senior counsel appearing for the filmmakers had assured that "Doosra" was not a biopic and that due permissions were taken from the appropriate right-holders to use certain clips involving the plaintiff.
On top of that, Ganguly's counsel apprehended a violation of the cricketer's personality rights, asserting that no licence was taken from him for the production of Doosra.

Set against the backdrop of India's famous 2002 NatWest Series victory over England, Doosra takes the image of Sourav Ganguly celebrating at Lord’s and gives it a different meaning. The movie follows Tara, a young girl who struggles to fit into her conservative household and begins questioning the expectations placed on her. When she watches his defiant celebration on television, his refusal to conform inspires her to find the courage to challenge the rules governing her own life, even if it means facing the consequences.

title: No football, no gym, no restaurants? Tiger Shroff shooting raises a FRIGHTENING question: Are Bollywood stars becoming PRISONERS of their own fame?
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

On Sunday, October 18, he was doing precisely that. It was supposed to be another ordinary evening. Tiger had finished playing football at a ground in Juhu and was preparing to leave when unidentified assailants opened fire near his vehicle. Tiger escaped unhurt, but his driver and a bystander were injured.

Adding to this, The incident has understandably raised questions about Bollywood’s security arrangements, the threats faced by prominent actors and the possible involvement of organised crime. But there is another question that deserves serious consideration.

Meanwhile, What happens when even the simplest activities in a Bollywood star’s life become potential security risks? And, perhaps more importantly, what does this mean for the culture of star photography that has become an inseparable part of Bollywood?

Notably, Imagine being unable to step outside your home without planning your movements, checking security arrangements or wondering whether somebody is watching. For most people, playing football, visiting a gym, meeting friends at a café or going out for dinner are ordinary activities. For celebrities, however, even these moments have increasingly become public events.

As per the latest buzz, The irony in Tiger’s case is particularly striking. Here is an star whose entire professional identity revolves around strength, agility, martial arts and performing extraordinary action sequences. On screen, he regularly overcomes seemingly impossible situations. Yet the real-life incident occurred after something as simple as a football game.

In further updates, The contrast is unsettling. No amount of physical fitness or martial arts training can eliminate the dangers posed by armed violence. And if an star begins to feel that an ordinary football outing requires extensive security arrangements, the implications extend far beyond one individual.

On top of that, What happens to the freedom to live spontaneously? Will actors eventually have to give up activities they have enjoyed for years? Will they have to restrict their movements to private facilities? Will something as simple as meeting friends require advance security coordination?

There was a time when seeing a movie star outside a cinema screen was a relatively rare experience. Today, star sightings have become an entertainment industry of their own. From airport arrivals and gym entrances to restaurant exits and family outings, virtually every movement of a major star is social-media content.

title: Tu Hai Meri Kiran review: The unique premise of Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal’s thriller deserved a better film
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Sometimes, a movie’s one-line premise is far more exciting than the actual plot. Tu Hai Meri Kiran, unfortunately, falls into that category.

Adding to this, Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal’s Tu Hai Meri Kiran rolled out in theatres on October 23. The premise Picture this: Kiran ( Sonakshi Sinha ), a popular author, is happily married to Riyaan (Ankit Gupta). One day, she discovers an old phone that turns out to be connected to another phone from the past, 10 years ago. Her call is answered by Samar ( Zaheer Iqbal ), who lives in 2016 and becomes obsessed with Kiran. He then sets out to change her past and insert himself into her life. What happens next forms the rest of the plot.

Meanwhile, Directed by Karan Rawal, the movie has a unique premise that keeps the tension alive, at least initially. The first half focuses on the two discovering the power they possess. Much of what today’s generation knows about time travel has been shaped by the Avengers and similar films. So, looking for logic in every time paradox is bound to disappoint. Tu Hai Meri Kiran is a Hindi commercial movie, after all, and takes certain cinematic liberties. But that is not the problem here.

Notably, The trouble begins when the movie’s idea becomes too complex for its own good. The second half keeps the viewer interested and does a decent job of explaining things as the narrative moves between 2016 and 2026. However, once the two realities begin to overlap, things start falling apart. Keeping track of what’s happening becomes a struggle after a point, and this confusion could affect the movie’s prospects with audiences. Karan, who has also written the movie, gets a little too ambitious with the climax and stretches the movie longer than what would have hit the sweet spot.

As per the latest buzz, Performance wise, Sonakshi delivers a good turn, while Zaheer makes for an interesting antagonist. Together, the two shoulder this tale of obsession effectively, even when the writing struggles to keep things together.

In further updates, Overall, for a movie about changing the past, Tu Hai Meri Kiran could certainly have done with a rethink. The premise is fresh enough to grab your attention, and Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal make a decent team. But the writing gets so caught up in its own twists that the story begins to lose its way. The second half, in particular, demands considerable attention without always rewarding it. In the end, the movie’s biggest problem isn’t time travel. It’s that the screenplay seems to have travelled a little too far from common sense.

On top of that, Rishabh Suri is an Assistant Editor, movie critic, and professional overthinker of plot points. He writes for HT City, keeping pace with an industry where news cycles expire long before the popcorn gets cold. He completed his graduation in English Honours from Kirori Mal College, followed by a Master’s degree in English Literature-effectively training his brain to over-analyse classic texts before applying those exact same skills to 3-hour Bollywood blockbusters. He got into the profession when he had barely graduated from college and has been at HT ever since. At HT, Rishabh reviews films with a simple rule: skip the dense academic jargon and get straight to the point. Beyond reviews, as Assistant Editor, he helps navigate the broader circus of showbiz, tracking everything from OTT shifts to sudden ticket-window panics. In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. When he isn’t writing against a deadline, he is usually sitting in a dark theater, compulsively memorising dialogues. For Rishabh, analysing movies isn't just a day job- it’s a habit he couldn't turn off even if he tried. Read More

In an exclusive interview with HT Lifestyle, Zaheer Iqbal reflects on his acting journey, his growing love for the craft and how his priorities have evolved since his Bollywood debut.

Adding to this, Zaheer Iqbal is all set to star in Karan Rawal’s psychological thriller Tu Hai Meri Kiran. Ahead of the movie’s rollout, he reflected on what drew him to the script and convinced him to take on this unconventional role. Notably, Speaking about the challenges of portraying his character, Zaheer shared, “Though I haven’t gone that deep into the psyche of the person, with workshops and direction, I was able to do justice to the character.”

title: Zee Studios sets February 5, 2027 release for Omung Kumar’s Silaa, starring Harshvardhan Rane
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Speaking about his journey as Virat, Harshvardhan Rane says, “ Silaa has been one of the most challenging and exciting journeys for me as an star. There is so much more to Virat than what meets the eye; he is a man driven by love, but when circumstances take an unexpected turn, he is pushed into a world where survival becomes just as important as finding the person he loves. The action, the locations and the emotional intensity of the movie demanded a lot from me, both physically and mentally. What really drew me to this story was the fact that beneath all the action and adventure, it is about how far you are willing to go for someone who means everything to you. I am excited for audiences to see this side of me on the big screen.”

Adding to this, On bringing this expansive world to life, director Omung Kumar adds, “With Silaa , we wanted to create a movie that takes audiences on a roller-coaster ride, where romance, action, mystery and adventure come together in an unexpected way. At its heart, the movie is about love and the lengths a person can go to when everything they believe in is put to the test. We wanted the world of the movie to feel expansive and visually striking, while ensuring that the emotions always remain at the centre of the story. Harshvardhan brings a certain intensity and physicality to Virat, while Sadia adds her own strength and depth to Silaa . Bringing this story to life was an exciting experience, and I hope audiences connect with its emotional core as much as they enjoy the scale and thrill of the movie.”
Meanwhile, A post shared by Bollywood Hungama🎥 (@realbollywoodhungama)

title: Exclusive| Doosra does not infringe any personality rights of Sourav Ganguly: Film's legal team
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Former Indian cricketer and captain Sourav Ganguly on moved to court to stay the rollout of the soon-to-release movie Doosra on October 23. He had filed the case over a violation of his personality rights. However, the Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to stay the rollout of the movie.

Adding to this, Sourav Ganguly In conversation with us, Madhu Gadodia, deputy managing partner of Naik Naik and company, the legal firm representing producer Masjda Sajeh and director Abhinay Deo told us, "The movie, Doosra is in theatres and is not a biopic on Sourav Ganguly. The movie tells the fictional story of Tara, a woman who challenges societal norms. The movie is not based on and does not infringe any rights of Mr. Ganguly. All match footage used in the movie has been duly licensed with appropriate permissions. The Delhi High Court, upon hearing the matter yesterday, was not inclined to stay the movie’s rollout. We will continue to defend the proceedings before the Court."

Meanwhile, Ganguly and Luv Films (who are making a biopic on Ganguly with Rajkummar Rao) argued that Doosra unlawfully exploits his identity and iconic career moments without consent, conflicting with their authorized biopic scheduled for May 2027. The plea specifically targeted the commercial use of his 2002 NatWest Series captaincy and his famous shirtless celebration on the Lord's balcony, arguing these are used strictly to drive ticket sales. Luv Films joined the suit based on an August 5, 2021 contract granting them exclusive global audiovisual rights to exploit Ganguly’s life story.

title: Abundantia aiON, in partnership with InVideo, announces its first film Beta Builder
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The movie is based on author Sukriti YJ’s novel ‘Beta Builder: Mumbai In The Metaverse’.

Adding to this, Beta Builder tells the story of Jai, a self-taught, genius architect from Dharavi who gets a chance to realise his dreams in the virtual reality world, only to discover that winning means far more than just proving himself. An underdog in every sense, Jai must fight the system that holds him back, win the love of his life, and give his community a voice in shaping its own future. Rooted in one of India's most iconic neighbourhoods and set against the limitless possibilities of a virtual world, Beta Builder is a story about ambition, belonging and what it truly means to build something that lasts.

Meanwhile, The movie is being developed and produced under Abundantia aiON's 'Human-First, AI-Empowered' creative philosophy, one that places human authorship and storytelling vision at the centre while harnessing AI across the production value chain, from development to screen.

Notably, Announcing the project, Vikram Malhotra, Founder and CEO of Abundantia Entertainment, shared, “ Beta Builder is everything aiON was built for, a story that begins in one of Mumbai's most iconic neighbourhoods and travels into a world that does not yet exist, told through technology that is rewriting what filmmaking can be. Jai's journey is about ambition, identity and the courage to build something bigger than yourself. It is a deeply human story, and the fact that it is being brought to life through AI makes it even more exciting to us. This is what Human-First, AI-Empowered means in practice. And this is just the beginning of what aiON and InVideo will build together."

As per the latest buzz, Beta Builder is the first in a slate of five AI-driven films being developed by Abundantia aiON in partnership with InVideo over the next three years. The broader aiON slate will span fully AI-generated features as well as live-action and AI hybrid productions, with titles beginning to roll out from the first quarter of 2027.

In further updates, Founded in 2013, Abundantia Entertainment's filmography includes Baby , Airlift , Toilet: Ek Prem Katha , Shakuntala Devi , Sherni , the Chhorii franchise, Breathe, Daldal, Subedaar and Maa Behen .

title: Madhur Bhandarkar announces Syama – The Missing Chapter on Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Titled Syama – The Missing Chapter (working title), the movie aims to bring the story of Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee to the big screen, revisiting his political journey, ideological beliefs and role in India's history.

Adding to this, A scholar and statesman, Dr. Mukherjee was a prominent political figure who advocated national unity. His journey included becoming the youngest Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta and serving in independent India's first Cabinet under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

Meanwhile, The movie will explore his ideological differences with the government, his decision to resign from the Cabinet and his role in founding the Bharatiya Jana Sangh in 1951. It will also revisit his 1953 campaign against the permit system in Jammu and Kashmir and the circumstances surrounding his death in detention.

Notably, Combining elements of historical drama and political thriller, Syama – The Missing Chapter seeks to examine the decisions and convictions that shaped Dr. Mukherjee's public life. The project also aims to revisit a chapter of India's political history and introduce his ideas and legacy to a new generation of viewers.

As per the latest buzz, Speaking about the project, producer Aditya Kumar Halwasiya shared, “Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee’s life is a powerful reminder that true leadership lies in courage, conviction and service to the nation. Through Syama , we aim to bring his remarkable journey to the screen and inspire a new generation to discover our history, embrace our heritage and understand the values that help shape our nation’s future,”

In further updates, Director Madhur Bhandarkar also shared his thoughts on the project and shared, “Exploring Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee’s life for the first time as a filmmaker is both a challenge and demanding. Through Syama , I hope to bring an important chapter of India’s history to the screen with honesty, sensitivity and a fresh perspective.”
On top of that, The movie is scheduled to go on floors next year, while further details about the cast and other aspects of the project remain under wraps.

title: Anupam Kher meets Stevie Wonder in Stockholm after concert, says ‘stardom may come and go, but kindness stays’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Anupam Kher had a night to remember in Stockholm after attending a live concert by music legend Stevie Wonder and meeting him backstage. The star later shared pictures from the evening on social media, talking about the experience of watching the singer perform and getting to interact with someone he has admired for years.

Adding to this, Anupam Kher calls meeting Stevie Wonder ‘surreal’, reveals what the music legend shared about him as an star. Anupam Kher is bowled over by Stevie Wonder’s performance Anupam was clearly moved by the concert, describing the atmosphere and Stevie Wonder’s performance in a heartfelt post. Sharing a glimpse of the evening, he wrote: "WONDERS OF WONDERS- AN EVENING WITH STEVIE WONDER. What an evening it was in Stockholm yesterday."

Meanwhile, The star spoke about how the singer kept the audience engaged with his music, describing the feeling of being in the same arena as the legendary performer. “One song after another, and with every note, Stevie Wonder seemed to fill the entire arena with magic. I don't think I can quite describe what it felt like to watch him perform so close! The music, the rhythm, every gesture, every nuance. It was a joy simply to be there, taking it all in,” he added.

Notably, View this post on Instagram The evening became even more memorable when the star met Wonder backstage. While he was excited to meet the Grammy-winning singer, he shared what stayed with him most was the musician’s kindness and the warmth he showed during their interaction. “And then came the surreal moment of meeting him backstage. I met not only a legendary singer, but also a humanitarian, a deeply kind man, and someone whose warmth and generosity touched me profoundly. The way he appreciated me as an star was so heartfelt. I left feeling grateful, humbled, and reminded that true greatness has a gentleness to it. Stardom may come and go, but kindness and grace stay with you,” the veteran star shared.

As per the latest buzz, He also acknowledged Brian Laroda, Wonder’s manager, for helping arrange the concert seats and making the backstage meeting possible. Thanking him for being part of such a special evening, the star wrote: “A heartfelt thank you to my friend Brian Laroda, Stevie's manager for arranging the wonderful seats and making this unforgettable meeting possible. I will always cherish the music, the evening, and the warmth of that moment. Some stars shine brightly for a lifetime. Some, like diamonds, are eternal. Jai Ho.”

In further updates, The meeting with Stevie Wonder comes weeks after hecaught up with his longtime friend, Hollywood star Robert De Niro, in New York. The star had travelled to the United States and Canada for his play Jaane Pehchaane Anjane and made time to meet De Niro during the trip.

On top of that, Anupam Kher is currently touring the US and Canada with his play Jaane Pehchane Anjaane. On the professional front, Anupam Kher was last seen in Tanvi The Great and will be starring in Khosla Ka Ghosla 2, set for 2027 rollout.

title: Ashoke Pandit says security cover for every star after attack on Tiger Shroff ‘not practical’: Everyone should feel safe, fear ko khatam karna hai
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The tension surrounding the recent assassination attempt on Tiger Shroff is still intact. As a measure of precaution, it’s even being speculated that the security arrangements for major celebs is being assessed. Amidst all this, to understand the sentiment within the industry, HT City spoke to Ashoke Pandit, chief advisor to Federation of Western India Cine Employees.

Adding to this, Ashoke Pandit; Jackie Shroff He says the fear was palpable initially, “Initially toh fear tha. But the government went all out and nabbed the accused in two days. That has proved how seriously the system took it. This increases our confidence. We are all very nice people in the industry, we are artists and performers, we are not violent people. Because the police has arrested, this will break the resolve of the attackers. The fear of law will build confidence in people.”

Meanwhile, Ashoke had also met Jackie Shroff , Tiger’s father, the very next day after the attack, at an event in Mumbai. We ask him about their interaction, “He (Jackie) shared ‘God has been kind, everything went off well. The government had reacted tremendously’ This gave him confidence and he went out to meet people, Tiger too met some. The authorities had got in touch with them immediately.”

Notably, As for the reports around the security cover for stars being increased, Ashoke continues, “It is not just about stars, it should be about the security of every individual. Kitne logon ko security denge? It is not practical. Ultimately effective steps should be taken for overall security of everyone. Fear ko khatam karna hai.”
As per the latest buzz, The industry, meanwhile goes on, “Work is on in full swing, kaam pe impact bilkul nahi dikh raha.”

In further updates, Rishabh Suri is an Assistant Editor, movie critic, and professional overthinker of plot points. He writes for HT City, keeping pace with an industry where news cycles expire long before the popcorn gets cold. He completed his graduation in English Honours from Kirori Mal College, followed by a Master’s degree in English Literature-effectively training his brain to over-analyse classic texts before applying those exact same skills to 3-hour Bollywood blockbusters. He got into the profession when he had barely graduated from college and has been at HT ever since. At HT, Rishabh reviews films with a simple rule: skip the dense academic jargon and get straight to the point. Beyond reviews, as Assistant Editor, he helps navigate the broader circus of showbiz, tracking everything from OTT shifts to sudden ticket-window panics. In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. When he isn’t writing against a deadline, he is usually sitting in a dark theater, compulsively memorising dialogues. For Rishabh, analysing movies isn't just a day job- it’s a habit he couldn't turn off even if he tried. Read More

title: CP, Nehru Place part of Delhi traffic advisory issued over protest march to ECI office
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory in view of a protest march to the Election Commission of India (ECI) office organised by ‘People Against SIR ’, a week-old alliance of students, farmers and civil society groups on Friday.

Adding to this, Traffic moves through Connaught Place as security was tightened. (Photo by Raj K Raj/ Hindustan Times) Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) leaders were also as per reports invited to join the march, from Bangla Sahib Gurdwara in Delhi's Connaught Place to Jantar Mantar.

Meanwhile, The march has been called to "restore democracy", demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and press for the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

title: Salman Khan breaks into a jig with Varun Dhawan mid speech; pulls Rashmika Mandanna's leg at IIFA 2027 event
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Salman Khan seemed in a jovial mood at an event in Mumbai on Thursday evening for IIFA 2027. Despite arriving at the venue flanked by heavy security, he seemed cheery as he interacted with Kareena Kapoor, Varun Dhawan and Rashmika Mandanna, who were also present, among other celebrities.

Adding to this, Salman Khan and Varun Dhawan at a press conference for the 27th International Indian Movie Academy (IIFA) Awards, in Mumbai. (PTI) Salman dances with Varun Dhawan, pulls Rashmika’s leg At the event, Varun was standing by Salman’s side as he spoke to the press. When Salman was asked if he had any tips for Varun to host the awards night, he joked, “Don’t host it. You’ll lose six hours just in hosting. It’s best you…come here,” he shared, asking Varun to join him in his impromptu dancing. “Just do this and leave. Let those who are pros at it do it.

Meanwhile, His jovial mood continued when Rashmika expressed happiness that next year would be her first IIFA performance. “This is my debut, guys, and I’m very, very excited, because…” she shared, even as Salman gestured that she’s happy due to the pay. Rashmika reiterated that she was excited as Salman pulled her leg about the money. He also joked that it took her so long to join them in performing at the awards show due to Sikandar.
Notably, Kareena Kapoor and Shahid Kapoor, who were also present on stage, couldn’t help but laugh along.

As per the latest buzz, On October 19, Tiger Shroff was shot at in Mumbai by two assailants. The incident left his driver and a bystander injured with bullet wounds. The star also sustained what looked like gunpowder burns. Later, an aide of gangster Lawrence Bishnoi took responsibility for the attack and claimed Tiger’s association with Salman as the reason. Ten suspects have been detained in the case so far, with three arrests made within hours of the shooting.

In further updates, Salman’s security has been beefed up since the incident, with the star grappling with Bishnoi and his gang for years now. title: At least 4 women injured in police tear gas shelling on anti-dam protesters in Arunachal Pradesh

title: ‘Industry has a bad reputation and karma’: Manoj Bajpayee says Bollywood has ‘ruined’ talented actors, admits only 25% of his potential has been used
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After years of delivering memorable performances, Manoj Bajpayee feels he has barely scratched the surface of what he can do as an star. He has criticised Bollywood for repeatedly typecasting performers, arguing that many gifted actors have been denied the roles and recognition they deserved. Speaking ahead of the rollout of his soon-to-release Netflix movie Gajab Raat , formerly titled Ghooskhor Pandat , Manoj reflected on his career and why he believes filmmakers have yet to fully harness his acting abilities.

Adding to this, ‘We have ruined talents’: Manoj Bajpayee calls out Bollywood’s typecasting, says only 25% of his talent was used. What the star shared about Bollywood In conversation with Zoom, Manoj Bajpayee spoke about how actors can get stuck playing the same kind of characters, leaving little room to explore their range. He feels the industry has let many gifted performers slip away without giving them the recognition or opportunities they deserved. Reflecting on his own journey, the star admitted that he, too, believes much of his potential remains untapped.

Meanwhile, “Stereotyping is for many actors, and we have ruined talents just by doing that in this industry. I have always maintained that this industry has a bad reputation and bad karma of demolishing such great talents by reducing them to nothing on the set, in terms of the roles, in terms of the treatment that they have given to them. Many of the people went away, withered away without any recognition. I have always maintained that only 25 percent of my acting abilities have been used; there’s a lot. But I think that’s an star’s greed or an star’s hunger, and I am very happy that the fire is still burning in the belly,” he shared.

Notably, While Manoj remains critical of the way Bollywood has treated actors in the past, he believes the arrival of streaming platforms has brought a significant change. He shared OTT has encouraged viewers to pay closer attention to performances and storytelling, making them more vocal about what works and what does not.

As per the latest buzz, "Mainly after the emergence of OTT here, things have changed drastically and we should always thank the coming of OTT in our country, and the families are watching. They can easily point it out and they talk about it in detail," he added.
In further updates, Manoj will next appear in Gajab Raat, reuniting with filmmaker Neeraj Pandey nearly a decade after working together on Aiyaary and the short movie Ouch.

On top of that, Produced by Friday Movie Works, the thriller is directed by Ritesh Shah and takes place over a single night. The story follows a police officer torn between personal interests and his duty, as one decision sets off a series of events with serious consequences. The movie marks Ritesh’s debut as a director and also stars Saqib Saleem, Akshay Oberoi, Divya Dutta, Kiku Sharda, Nushrratt Bharuccha and Shraddha Das. Gajab Raat will premiere globally on Netflix on October 23.

title: 12-hour shutdown hits 3 Arunachal Pradesh districts over 10 detained dam protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A 12-hour shutdown was observed across three districts of Arunachal Pradesh on Friday over the demand for the rollout of 10 protesters detained for opposing the construction of a large dam on the Siang River, disrupting normal life, transportation and commercial activities.

Adding to this, Protesters demand halt to surveys and consultation of a large dam on the Siang River (Utpal Parashar) The shutdown was called by the Adi Bane Kebang United (ABKU), in collaboration with SAYA, the Adi Galo Welfare Society, SIFF and SIFFYW, across Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts from 5 am to 5 pm.

Meanwhile, As per the latest buzz, the 10 individuals were taken into custody by the state administration around 20 days ago following protests against the proposed dam project in Upper Siang district . Various organisations have repeatedly demanded their rollout, alleging that the authorities have failed to take effective action.
Notably, The organisations have warned that if all 10 detained protesters are not rolled out within the next 24 hours, they will intensify their agitation, potentially by calling a wider shutdown.
As per the latest buzz, The shutdown affected travellers moving to and from different parts of the country, including Assam , with people seeking medical treatment among those facing difficulties.

In further updates, A man travelling from Odisha to obtain medicine for his mother, who has liver cancer, told reporters that he was unaware of the shutdown and was left stranded after a checkpost was closed and his bus turned back.

On top of that, “I didn't know about any issue. I arrived here this morning. The checkpost was closed, so the bus turned back, leaving us stranded here,” he shared, appealing to the shutdown organisers to provide exemptions for medical emergencies and students appearing for examinations.
A woman travelling from Siliguri with two other patients also described the difficulties caused by the shutdown.

title: Annamalai says CJP has right to protest in India, disagrees with its tactics
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamala i on Friday shared his organisation, We The Leaders, does not support the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) because of differences in their objectives, but backed the group's right to protest.

Adding to this, K Annamalai shared that objectives of 'We The Leaders' movement is completely different from those of CJP (ANI) “If you ask whether our ‘We The Leaders’ will support the CJP party, we will never do so. Because our goal is different, and their goal is different. However, if you ask whether the CJP party has the right to protest in India, yes, it does,” he shared at an event on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Annamalai had earlier described CJP's protest tactics as “misguided”, while asserting that the group had the right to oppose issues it considered important.

Notably, “As I mentioned yesterday, I might not agree with the tactics of the CJP, and I think many of theirs are misguided. But if you ask me whether they have a right to oppose/argue/protest on an issue that they think is important, I would categorically say — YES,” he shared in a post on X on October 21.
As per the latest buzz, Annamalai's remarks come amid a row over the Delhi Police's handling of CJP's protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

In further updates, In conversation with reporters in Chennai earlier this week, the former BJP leader criticised the police for detaining protesters, arguing that the action could strengthen the group's leadership rather than weaken it.

On top of that, “To arrest them for a violation and again to drag them in terms of how they spend their time in jail, that is only going to make the leaders of CJP stronger. I'm afraid of it. The Delhi Police are doing a real disservice,” he shared .

A day after making these remarks, Annamalai shared he had faced social media trolling over his comments. He also questioned the restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar and raised concerns about the powers exercised by police officials in cases involving preventive detention.

title: My 20s were avoidable: Comedian Sumukhi Suresh on exploring dating, female friendship in 'Hoemonal'
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

New Delhi, Comedian Sumukhi Suresh was just coming out of a long-term relationship when she got the idea for "Hoemonal", her new Netflix special, which she describes as a "chick-flick" about a conservatively-raised woman.

Adding to this, My 20s were avoidable: Comedian Sumukhi Suresh on exploring dating, female friendship in 'Hoemonal' A multi-hyphenate artiste, Suresh is known as a writer, comedian and star who switches easily between her different identities. The special, she shared, is about women like her, who are earning money and now feel "guilty about spending it".

Meanwhile, "I think 'Hoemonal' on Netflix is a proper comfort chick-flick/rom-com that you will watch and keep watching. It's about a conservatively-raised girl because I was raised very conservatively. I was with someone for a really long time. And then that ended.

Notably, "And suddenly I was like, 'Oh, I have to start dating'. And I have never experienced those things. So, it is a conservatively-raised girl failing to be a hoe while managing her hormones," Suresh told PTI in an interview.

As per the latest buzz, In the over-one-hour-long show, the comedian talks about breaking up, spectacularly failing to figure out dating apps, female friendships and how she was raised to be a "sindoor chaser".
In further updates, Suresh shared when she was asked what her target audience for the special was, she shared "25 and above" but those in their 20s are also welcome.

On top of that, "I think my 20s were very avoidable. I actually started enjoying life at 30. I feel like most women are living their 20s in their 30s. The earlier idea was that you study, graduate, have a job and then any minute you will find someone or you will be partnered up. And then a good chunk went, 'Maybe I don't want to.' And then you start building your life... So, I feel like I was a teenager, then I came directly to my 30s," Suresh shared.
The comedian, who wrote and starred in the popular two-season comedy drama series "Pushpavalli" in 2017, shared she loves the energy of live performances.

title: IMA seeks review of Sunny Deol starrer Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak; raises concerns over portrayal of doctors and hospital violence
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The association has urged authorities to examine the movie’s depiction of alleged corruption in healthcare and scenes involving assaults on medical professionals.

Adding to this, The IMA has outlined four key areas of concern, including the generalisation of alleged misconduct across the medical fraternity, the depiction of physical assaults on healthcare workers, the safety of medical personnel and the potential impact on doctor-patient trust.

Meanwhile, In its letter, the association cautioned against portraying individual instances of wrongdoing in a manner that could reflect on the wider medical community. It shared, "The portrayal risks creating the impression that corruption, unethical practices, and alleged corruption in medical fraternity. While individual misconduct must be investigated and punished, the actions of a few must not be used to tarnish the reputation of countless honest and dedicated doctors."

Notably, The organisation also expressed concern over scenes involving physical confrontations in medical facilities, particularly if such actions are presented as justified. The IMA shared, "Scenes depicting physical assaults on doctors, nursing staff, and hospital personnel, particularly when presented as heroic or justified acts, risk normalising violence against those committed to saving lives."

As per the latest buzz, Highlighting the safety concerns faced by healthcare workers, the association further shared, "Doctors and healthcare personnel already face serious safety challenges in hospitals. Content that appears to glorify attacks on medical professionals may encourage hostility and further endanger those providing essential healthcare services."

In further updates, The IMA also flagged the possible impact of such portrayals on public confidence in medical professionals, stating, "Such portrayals may foster unwarranted mistrust and hostility towards doctors, weakening the mutual trust and cooperation essential for effective treatment and healthcare delivery."

On top of that, While making its objections known, the association clarified that it does not support unethical medical practices and that individual cases of misconduct should be addressed through statutory and disciplinary mechanisms. It argued that such instances should not lead to broad portrayals that could affect the reputation of the profession or discourage aspiring medical students.

As part of its appeal, the IMA requested an impartial review of the movie’s content and asked for appropriate corrective measures to address its concerns. It also called on the relevant authorities to consider further action, stating, "In view of these concerns, we respectfully request... [an] impartial review of the movie's content and its portrayal of the medical profession; seek appropriate corrective measures from the filmmakers to address the generalisation of alleged misconduct and the depiction of violence against healthcare workers; [and] consider a ban or other appropriate action if justified under applicable law."

title: Bharatiya Kisan Union leader Rakesh Tikait stages sit-in after finding Ganna Bhawan locked
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Bharatiya Kisan Union ( BKU ) leader Rakesh Tikait staged a sit-in outside the gate of the Ganna Kisan Sansthan (Ganna Bhawan) in Dalibagh on Thursday after finding the institute locked.

Adding to this, Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) leader Rakesh Tikait sits on a dharna in protest against the closure of gates at the Ganna Sansthan premises on the eve of his proposed 'Kisan-Mazdoor Mahapanchayat' (PTI Photo/Nand Kumar) The incident took place when Tikait reached the institute ahead of Kisan Mazdoor Mahapanchayat scheduled on Friday. Finding the gate closed, Tikait and his supporters sat on the ground outside the gate itself.
Meanwhile, After the protest, the administration started the process of opening the gate, sources shared. The gates were opened at around 8pm, shared Alok Varma, district president of the BKU.

Notably, The sit-in was linked to Friday’s proposed mahapanchayat of farmers at Ganna Sansthan. The proposed Mahapanchayat is expected to see participation of farmers from Western UP, Terai and Central UP. It is being seen as a show of strength by the BKU faction led by Tikait ahead of 2027 assembly polls.

As per the latest buzz, Sitting by the roadside, Tikait shared that if the gate is not opened, the panchayat will be held on the road itself. “If you lock the gate of the institution for farmers, where will farmers go? We will hold the panchayat here on the road,” Tikait shared.

In further updates, BKU workers shared mahapanchayat has been called to raise key demands: increase sugarcane price to ₹ 500-600 per quintal, immediate clearance of pending dues by sugar mills, increase in circle rate for land acquisition and legal guarantee for MSP.
On top of that, The Dalibagh-situated Ganna Kisan Sansthan is a traditional venue for farmers’ meetings in Lucknow and is linked to sugarcane farmers’ interests.

Police force was deployed on the spot as Tikait’s sit-in drew a crowd of supporters. Officials shared that the situation is under control and permission for Friday’s panchayat is being examined. Tikait, who has been mobilising farmers over cane price and payment issues ahead of the crushing season, shared farmers are being forced to protest for basic demands.

title: Ramayana vs Adipurush: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash-starrer dwarfs Prabhas film, outpaces it by 120% in advance bookings
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ticket sales for Nitesh Tiwari’s ambitious Ramayana adaptation began on Dussehra, 15 days before the movie's rollout in theatres ahead of Diwali. Giving the movie such a long advance booking window seems to be the makers’ strategy to increase the buzz around it. And early signs indicate that the strategy seems to be working. Ramayana Part One is showing breakneck pre-sales, crossing one lakh tickets with 13 days to go before rollout.

Adding to this, Ramayana is outpacing Adipurush by a mile in advance bookings. In doing so, it has also outpaced the previous big-scale Ramayana adaptation, Adipurush, which had a grand opening before it crash-landed due to extremely negative word of mouth.

Meanwhile, Advance bookings for Adipurush began five days before its rollout, in line with how most big Indian films do so. The pre-sales Hindi version opened first, followed by the Telugu version a day later. In the first 24 hours, Adipurush sold around 36K tickets for its Hindi version, bringing in ₹ 1.40 crore rupees in pre-sales. This was a healthy number. As the Telugu advance booking opened the following day, the pre-sales soared.

Notably, Ramayana has followed a similar pattern. The first day saw ticket sales only for the Hindi version, as the Kannada version opened with just 60 shows across India. Despite that, Ramayana sold over 65K tickets, minting ₹ 3.13 crore rupees in gross on its opening day. This figure is 123% higher than what Adipurush managed in the same time period. The Prabhas-starrer salvaged its pre-sales with the Telugu advance bookings in the days to come, closing its final figure at a respectable ₹ 26 crore rupees, with over a million tickets sold.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana has already reached the ₹ 6.25 crore rupees mark. The Kannada, Telugu, and Tamil versions have barely begun, contributing just ₹ 50 lakh to this figure. The Hindi version of Ramayana is already showing occupancy of 15-20% in most major cities, with over 900 screens open. In comparison, the Kannada version has opened in fewer than 100 screens so far and is still doing well, with some centres already reporting up to 72% occupancy for the morning shows. Yash’s star power will help the movie soar to greater heights once advance bookings for Kannada and Telugu open fully later this month.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

On top of that, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.

title: Udta Teer review: This Ayushmann Khurrana spy comedy rarely misses a chance to make you laugh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Udta Teer's sharp first half and talented cast make the absurd premise sing, though a more serious second half and pace-slowing songs dull the momentum. Cast: Ayushmann Khurrana, Sara Ali Khan, Ram Kapoor

Adding to this, I am struggling to recall the last time a movie made me laugh as much as Udta Teer did. And none of it relies on double meaning dialogues or cheap innuendo, mind you. If you can sense my excitement already, let's get straight to why this Ayushmann Khurrana starrer simply works.

Meanwhile, Directed by Akash Kaushik (who has previously written the screenplays for hits like Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 and 3) Udta Teer follows Bilal/Vikrant (Ayushmann), who has been working as a Pakistani spy in India's counter terrorism unit. One day, he loses his memory in an accident and ends up working for India instead, dismantling Pakistan's terror network embedded within the system. Akash was bang on when he of late described the movie as a "reverse Dhurandhar ".

Notably, Making his feature directorial debut with Udta Teer, Akash proves surprisingly sure footed. Also the movie's writer, he keeps the first half tight, with hardly a scene feeling like dead weight. The pacing is spot on, with witty one liners and funny situations keeping the laughs coming. There is Pakistan bashing, but not the chest thumping kind. The humour is far more cheeky than jingoistic. Take Gulshan Grover's character, for instance, who declares that the head of the Pakistani Army never has to bow his head before anyone-- until the President of China calls and he bows his head immediately. A man waiting every day for the Pakistani Army General to give him the time of the day in Gulshan's office, turns out to be the Pakistani Prime Minister himself. All this lands because the movie knows exactly where to poke fun, and more importantly, when to stop.

As per the latest buzz, After such a funny first half, the second half naturally comes with high expectations. This is where Udta Teer changes gears, and not to its advantage. As the movie tries to tie up its plot, the narrative becomes more serious than you might have bargained for, taking some of the fizz out. The momentum built in the first half begins to dip, and you find yourself missing the earlier ability for turning even the most absurd situations into laugh out loud moments.
In further updates, There are also some moments, like the placement of a romantic and patriotic song, which slows down the pace.
On top of that, But does that mean Udta Teer derails completely? Nope. In fact, it leaves you wishing this were the start of a franchise, because there is plenty of potential here.

A big reason it works is its talented cast, which makes even the most absurd ideas seem normal. From making Rahul Bose dance to It's the Time to Disco while lying in a vegetative state in a hospital, to turning heartrate monitor beeps into the tune of an iconic Dharma song, there is plenty to enjoy. Ayushmann Khurrana is pitch perfect as Bilal, the spy grappling with memory loss. He gets the balance between confusion and comedy just right. The late Mukul Dev gives him tough competition, bringing an effortless sense of humour to his role. Sandeep Anand is hilarious as Bilal's cook, while Suhail Nayyar is equally good as Bilal's best friend. Sara Ali Khan, as Bilal's wife, has a decent role and she does well.

title: Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar review: This Luv Ranjan-coded buddy romance with newcomers is a fun, harmless ride for the most part
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar's light comedy and lively climax have their moments, but thin plotting and unconvincing romances make it difficult to root for the characters. Cast: Sparsh, Alisha, Kunal, Sakshi, Tushar and Sargun

Adding to this, Good looking people, catchy songs, scenic locations and cheesy dialogues. For decades, Indian cinema has relied on this tried and tested formula to tell rom coms, and audiences have rarely complained. Luv Ranjan, however, found his own spin on it 15 years ago, throwing in bickering friends and everyday lingo that made Pyaar Ka Punchnama and Sonu Ke Titu Ki Sweety big successes. Now comes Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar , another attempt to revisit familiar territory. Does it have enough charm to make an old formula feel fresh?

Meanwhile, Directed by Anun Saini, the movie follows three school friends- Shivi, Gautam and Vedant, who are now colleagues, all single and still searching for love. A school reunion brings with it a chance of finally confessing their feelings to their respective school crushes. But when it comes to matters of the heart, is a second chance all it takes or are some things best left in the past?

Notably, For starters, there is an ease to the way this roughly 2 hour 20 minute movie begins. Luv Ranjan and Jehan Handa, who have written PPDB, keep things light and tap into what rarely fails: nostalgia. Here, it is the nostalgia of going back to school and meeting classmates you have long lost touch with. Set against the beautiful landscapes of Dehradun, the movie is easy on the eyes.

As per the latest buzz, The first half of PPDB is a breeze, largely thanks to the chemistry between its three leads. A few dips too surface along the way. But a major problem crops up soon: for all its easy charm, what is the movie actually about? The characters go back to school, meet their respective crushes... and then what? The movie seems unsure of where to go from there.

In further updates, The second half picks up the pace, and the movie finally seems to find some direction. The climax works, wrapping things up on a fun note. The comedy lands more often than it misses, with a handful of sequences likely to draw genuine chuckles. Thankfully, the dialogues steer clear of recycled WhatsApp jokes, giving the humour a more natural feel. A major track feels hard to buy into- a man falling head over heels for a school crush he barely spoke to back in the day, expects her to call off her impending wedding years later, all within two days of the reunion! Nostalgia can make old memories feel special, but it cannot, by itself make a convincing love story.

On top of that, The music by Rochak Kohli is very good, and helps the movie a lot. The acting performances by the newcomers- Sparsh Walia, Sakshi Vaidya, Kunal Vaid, Alisha Chopra (as Gehna) and Tushar Chhibber (as Kabir) are good, and lift the wafer thin story. Sparsh's character reminds you of Kartik Aaryan from the first Pyaar Ka Punchnama.

Overall, Pehla Pyaar Doosri Baar has its moments. Its characters are busy chasing the people they fancied in school, but the movie never quite makes you root for these romances as much as it should. That shared, watch it with your friends and the familiar setting might get you talking about the people you fancied and the confessions you never made. Your stories might just be better written than this one.

title: Aamir Khan breaks down in tears talking about career's weakest moments, says he lost relationships, time with kids by working like a ‘madman’
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Star Aamir Khan was reduced to tears on stage at the Singapore International Movie Festival on Thursday as he recalled the weakest moments of his acting career. The star spoke about how three decades of nonstop work had cost him years with his family.

Adding to this, Aamir Khan was honoured at the Singapore International Movie Festival on Thursday. (File Photo) (PTI) Aamir Khan breaks down talking about career On Thursday, at the Singapore movie festival, the Bollywood superstar was awarded the Screen Icon Award by renowned Hong Kong-based movie director Peter Chan Ho-sun. Later in the evening, Aamir sat down for a chat about his life and work in a conversation session moderated by Singapore comedian Rishi Budhrani.

Meanwhile, When asked about the weakest moment in his career, Aamir responded, “When I was sitting in COVID, and I was thinking, I shared, about 30 years have passed of my life. And it’s okay to work like a madman, completely obsessed with what you’re doing for one year, two years, five years. But if it goes on for 30 years, I mean, you’ve lost your relationships. Your kids have grown up; they’re adults now. So I felt a deep sense of loss.”

Notably, Aamir then paused while speaking and broke down in tears. The star then apologised to the audience before gathering himself as the crowd broke into applause. Wiping his tears away, Aamir added that the experience pushed him to make a major change, and that for the last four years he has deliberately carved out time for his family and close friends. “I’m so glad that this thought occurred to me when I was 56 and not when I was 86, when it would be really too late to do anything about it,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, In the same answer about his weakest moments, Aamir Khan recounted an earlier low point from the start of his career. After his 1988 debut Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak was a huge success, Aamir recalled signing nine films within six months. However, he realised his mistake once filming began. Aamir shared he would come home and weep to his then-wife Reena. The films then flopped one after another, and he was branded a “one-movie wonder.”
In further updates, “At that time, mentally and emotionally, I felt like I was in quicksand. I was sinking slowly, and the more I struggled to get out, the deeper I was going,” Aamir added.

On top of that, Accepting the Screen Icon Award, Aamir Khan thanked the festival and shared that having Chan present it made the moment special. “Filmmaking is a collective art form, and a lot of people contribute to each other’s work,” he shared. Aamir last attended the festival nine years ago with his production Secret Superstar. This year, he also has a 25th anniversary screening of Lagaan, his first movie as producer, lined up at the festival.

Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More
